stories.title: Cricketer Abhishek Sharma objects to fans taking selfies in Jaipur:SRH batter says, 'turn off the mobile phone' while visiting Govind Dev Ji temple ahead of IPL match
stories.summary: Before the IPL match in Jaipur, Sunrisers Hyderabad player Abhishek Sharma visited Govind Dev Ji Temple with his mother. Even though he was wearing a white mask, fans recognized him and began taking photos and videos. During this, he stopped one fan and asked them to turn off the camera. A crowd gathered around him inside the temple premises, making him seem slightly uncomfortable. However, at the insistence of some fans, he agreed to take selfies. Earlier, he had sat at the temple entrance with his mother to offer prayers and attend the aarti. Later, he was seen helping his mother through the crowd while leaving. Abhishek Sharma’s team Sunrisers Hyderabad is set to face Rajasthan Royals on April 25 at Sawai Mansingh Stadium. He had arrived in Jaipur with his mother on April 22 for the match. PHOTOS of the cricketer at Govind Dev Ji Temple Abhishek told a fan, ‘Turn off the mobile phone’ Fans became excited after spotting Abhishek Sharma at the temple. Although he was wearing a white mask, fans recognized him. Many then tried to take selfies with him, but security personnel stopped them. Fans began taking selfies and making videos from a distance, after which Abhishek intervened and asked them to stop. Looked uncomfortable in the crowd, fans still took selfies Abhishek Sharma appeared uneasy amid the crowd inside the temple premises. He completed the circumambulation (parikrama) of Govind Dev Ji Temple while surrounded by devotees. Earlier, he and his mother were welcomed by members of the temple committee. Priests conducted the prayer rituals through him, and he was also presented with a symbolic memento of Govind Dev Ji. Abhishek is in Jaipur for the match against Rajasthan Royals Abhishek Sharma is currently in Jaipur for an IPL match. He arrived in Jaipur on April 22 with his mother. Abhishek Sharma is present here with the Sunrisers Hyderabad team. The team's match will be played against Rajasthan Royals at Sawai Mansingh Stadium on April 25. During his Jaipur visit, he took religious darshan and received blessings before the match.

stories.title: Gorakhpur club owner’s son shoots himself, dies:40-year-old reaches farmhouse, makes call before taking his own life
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, Ambarish (40), son of billionaire businessman and Gorakhpur Club operator Atul Srivastava, died by suicide. On Friday, he shot himself in the mouth with his licensed pistol and died on the spot. Ambarish reached his farmhouse alone in his Fortuner at around 8 am on Friday. He was speaking to someone on his mobile when he went upstairs. Between 8:30 am and 9 am, he shot himself. Hearing the gunshot, the farmhouse staff rushed upstairs and found his body lying in a pool of blood. However, the family claims that Ambarish was cleaning his pistol when it accidentally went off. Body found by staff, pistol recovered Farmhouse staff rushed to the spot and found Ambrish lying in a pool of blood. He had sustained a gunshot injury to the face, and a pistol was found in his hand. He was declared dead at the scene. The reason behind the suicide is not yet known. Police and forensic teams investigating Senior Superintendent of Police Dr. Kaustubh reached the spot soon after receiving information. Police have begun questioning staff members, while a forensic team is collecting evidence from the scene. Business background and family details Ambrish lived on Park Road in Gorakhpur and was involved in the tent house business, along with contract work. His company, AK Tent House, was known for providing arrangements at major political and VVIP events. His farmhouse in Kusmhi is located around 10 km from his residence and includes a warehouse on the third floor. Recent public role and family Ambrish was recently elected as the General Secretary of the Shri Chitragupt Temple Sabha. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had attended the oath-taking ceremony of the newly elected office bearers. He is survived by his two young sons, aged 8 and 10. His younger brother Ranu is also a businessman. His father, Atul Srivastava, has previously served as the president of the same temple committee.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath to inaugurate Rashmirathi festival today:Three-day celebration marks 75 years of Dinkar’s work
stories.summary: A three-day literary and cultural festival, Rashmirathi Parv, will be held in Lucknow from April 24 to 26 to commemorate 75 years of Rashmirathi, the iconic work by national poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate the event on Friday, while Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will attend as the keynote speaker. The festival aims to bring together literature, national discourse, and cultural expression on a single platform. Indira Gandhi Pratishthan to host the event The grand event will take place at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, where literary figures, scholars, and youth from across the country will participate. The objective is to introduce Dinkar’s literary legacy to the younger generation and strengthen discussions around nationalism and cultural identity. Day 1: National seminar and Theatrical performance The inaugural day (April 24) will begin with the launch of the souvenir Rashmirathi Samvad. This will be followed by a national seminar where scholars will discuss Dinkar’s literary contributions, his ideas on nationalism, and their relevance in contemporary times. In the evening, a stage adaptation based on Rashmirathi will be performed, serving as a major attraction for attendees. Day 2: Focus on Swami Vivekananda’s vision On April 25, discussions will center on the role of Swami Vivekananda in shaping India’s cultural identity. The sessions will aim to inspire youth with messages of self-confidence, national service, and spiritual awareness. A cultural evening will feature a theatrical presentation based on Vivekananda’s life. Day 3: Tribute to Tilak and Atal Bihari Vajpayee The concluding day (April 26) will include discussions on the contributions of Bal Gangadhar Tilak and former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee to nation-building. The event will also feature Atal Swarajali, a musical tribute based on Vajpayee’s poems, along with a theatrical performance on Lokmanya Tilak. Inspiration for youth and cultural pride According to Tourism Minister Jaiveer Singh, the festival is designed to inspire youth with values such as patriotism, self-respect, perseverance, and social harmony. Through Rashmirathi Parv, Uttar Pradesh aims to showcase not only its developmental progress but also its rich cultural heritage.

stories.title: 'If we feel like burden, say it clearly':Ex-MP Brij Bhushan Singh asserts to show relevance of Kshatriya community ahead of 2027 UP polls
stories.summary: Former Kaiserganj MP and BJP leader Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on Thursday delivered a strong and combative message, saying that if political parties consider him and his community irrelevant, they should state it openly. Singh asserted that the response would be evident in the upcoming state elections. Speaking at the Babu Veer Kunwar Singh Vijay Utsav held at Town Hall in Bhagalpur, Bihar, Singh, without naming any party, accused governments of ignoring certain sections of society and raised concerns about the perceived neglect of the Kshatriya community. “Tell us if we are no longer needed” “Today, in the eyes of governments, we have no existence. If anyone thinks we have become a burden, just say it once—that we are no longer needed. Say it in 2027 or 2029. We will show whether we are relevant or not,” Singh said. He added that the time for persuasion is over and that communities must now recognise and assert their own strength. Call for self-reflection within community Urging introspection, Singh said that the community’s silence in the past had led to its marginalisation. “Whenever we were suppressed, we remained silent. That is why we are not given importance today,” he remarked. He also said that society had failed to secure due recognition for historical figures such as Veer Kunwar Singh, Maharaja Devi Baksh Singh, Rani Lakshmibai, and Birsa Munda. “Credit for freedom limited to a few” Singh alleged that the credit for India’s independence has been confined to a select few, while many revolutionaries have been overlooked. Referring to popular narratives, he remarked that only certain slogans gained prominence, sidelining the ,contributions of others. Quoting a Hindi couplet, he said that those who remain neutral and silent during critical times also bear responsibility, adding that societal silence had proved costly. Questions raised over constitution credit narrative The former MP also questioned the common perception surrounding the framing of the Constitution. He noted that the Constituent Assembly had 242 members, not just Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and claimed that Bihar had the highest representation at the time. “If anyone disagrees, they are welcome to debate,” he said, calling for a broader recognition of contributions. “Society has lost relevance in government’s eyes” Appealing for introspection, Singh said that if society had followed the ideals of figures like Lord Ram, Bappa Rawal, and Maharana Pratap, it would not be seen as irrelevant today. He reiterated that governments currently do not recognise the community’s significance. Reference to 2023 controversy Referring to past controversies, Singh claimed that he was the target of a “global conspiracy” in 2023 but refused to bow down. Quoting poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, he stressed courage and resilience. He also recited lines from the Hanuman Chalisa, stating that a follower of such ideals would not easily submit. “Time to recognise strength, not seek validation” Concluding his address, Singh urged the Kshatriya community to focus on building strength through power, intellect, and knowledge. “This is not the time to keep explaining ourselves, but to recognise our strength,” he said, adding that there is no need for fear or despair.

stories.title: UP temperature soars to 44.4°C amid heatwave:Elephant seen bathing repeatedly; 40 districts face heatwave alert
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh continues to reel under intense heatwave conditions, with scorching temperatures and strong sunlight since Friday morning. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a heatwave alert for 40 districts and a “warm night” alert for 17 districts, indicating little to no relief even during nighttime. Temperature may cross 45°C, rain likely after April 26 According to the IMD, severe heat conditions will persist for the next two days, with temperatures likely to cross 45°C. However, from April 26 onwards, a change in weather is expected, bringing thunderstorms and light rainfall over a four-day period. Meteorologist Atul Singh from Lucknow said that a new weather disturbance will become active from April 26, increasing cloud activity across the state. Initial drizzle is expected in western Uttar Pradesh and Terai regions, followed by thunderstorms and rain statewide. Temperatures may drop by 2–3°C, with fluctuating weather conditions likely until April 29. 4 pictures of the weather Animals struggle as heat intensifies The heatwave is also affecting animals. At Gorakhpur Zoo, an elephant has been seen repeatedly bathing itself to stay cool. In Lucknow Zoo, arrangements such as ice blocks, coolers, and sprinklers have been made for animals. In Kanpur, special provisions like Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) are being given to tigers to help them cope with the heat. Man dies in Kanpur amid heatwave In Kanpur, a 45-year-old man, Sunil Kumar, died while riding pillion on a moving motorcycle. Family members and locals suspect that extreme heat exposure led to his death. Precautionary measures in several districts In view of rising temperatures, authorities in Agra, Mathura, Firozabad, and Mainpuri have banned outdoor labour work between 12 pm and 4 pm to prevent heat-related illnesses. 30 districts cross 40°C, Banda hottest Over the past 24 hours, temperatures in 30 districts of the state have crossed 40°C. Banda recorded the highest temperature at 44.4°C, making it the hottest location in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: 2 terror suspects linked to Pakistani gangsters arrested:Accused plotted target killings for ₹3 lakh
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) on Thursday arrested two suspected terrorists from Noida, alleging links with Pakistani gangsters and intelligence operatives. Officials said the accused were in contact with handlers across the border and were attempting to build a sleeper cell network in India through social media platforms. According to the ATS, the duo was planning targeted killings using hand grenades, allegedly aiming at specific individuals, with a deal of ₹3 lakh struck for carrying out the attacks. Accused identified, linked to Pakistani operatives During interrogation, one of the accused identified himself as Tushar Chauhan, also known as Hizbullah Ali Khan, a resident of Meerut, while the other, Sameer Khan, is from Delhi. Investigators said both were in contact with Pakistani gangsters Shahzad Bhatti and Abid Jatt. Authorities also claimed that radical Pakistan-based social media influencers were being used to target and influence Indian youth online. Radicalisation and direct contact through social media Tushar reportedly told investigators that he came under the influence of certain individuals and social media content, which gradually drew him toward extremist ideology. During this period, he connected with Shahzad Bhatti and Abid Jatt via Instagram. Their communication later escalated to voice calls, video chats, and push-to-talk platforms. To gain Bhatti’s trust, Tushar allegedly created social media accounts in his name and reconnected even after earlier accounts were blocked. Eventually, he obtained Bhatti’s phone number and began direct communication. Cash incentives and assurances of support Tushar claimed that Bhatti assigned him the task of throwing grenades at specific residences to carry out killings. He was allegedly promised modern weapons and financial incentives—₹50,000 upfront and ₹2.5 lakh after completing the operation. He further stated that he was assured assistance in obtaining a passport and being routed to Pakistan via Dubai. Investigators said references to intelligence agency operatives were also made to reinforce the instructions. A pistol and some cash recovered from him are believed to have been supplied through this network. Co-accused tasked with propaganda activities Sameer Khan was also allegedly in contact with Bhatti through encrypted communication channels. He was assigned the task of writing “TTH” (Tehreek-e-Taliban Hindustan) on public walls and recruiting others into the network. Officials said Sameer and Tushar connected via Instagram and later jointly conducted reconnaissance of potential targets assigned by their handlers. Authorities believe both were prepared to execute the planned attacks. Threats issued, legal action initiated The ATS stated that the accused had issued death threats to several individuals, sometimes during conference calls where Pakistani handlers were also present. Based on digital evidence recovered from their mobile phones and preliminary interrogation, investigators concluded that both were involved in anti-national activities and were preparing to carry out attacks in India under instructions from a Pakistan-based network. A case has been registered at the ATS police station in Lucknow under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Arms Act, and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Both accused have been produced in court, and further legal proceedings are underway.

stories.title: ₹30 lakh extorted via ‘digital arrest’ scam:Fraud began with fake FedEx call, accused posed as narcotics officials; 2 arrested
stories.summary: Gwalior State Cyber Police have busted a major network involved in fraud under the pretext of “digital arrest” and Telegram trading, arresting two accused. The accused used to impersonate officials from FedEx and the Narcotics Control Bureau to intimidate people and extort lakhs of rupees. Complainant Harshit Dwivedi said the accused called him claiming drugs and illegal items were found in his parcel. The call was then transferred to a supposed narcotics officer. By creating fear of “digital arrest”, they got ₹30,25,719 transferred in the name of “police clearance”. After the complaint, police arrested Saurabh Kumar (24), a resident of Lakhimpur Kheri, and Rajesh Kumar (27). Cyber police traced the accused using fake IP addresses, bank transactions and digital evidence. They were arrested after a raid in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh. Investigation revealed that the accused opened fake bank accounts to route the fraud money. Transactions worth crores from 16 states were found in these accounts. Around ₹10 lakh from the complainant was directly transferred to the accused’s account. According to police, the accused first posed as courier company employees and then scared victims by claiming drugs were found in parcels. The call was then connected to a fake officer. Through video calls, victims were threatened with “digital arrest” and made to transfer money. Network Spread Across the Country The probe revealed the gang’s network was spread across Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. The accused kept changing locations to evade arrest. Police-Government Agencies Don't Ask for Money on Video Calls Police clarified that no government agency demands money over phone or video calls and there is no legal provision like “digital arrest”. In such cases, people should immediately report on cyber helpline 1930 and never share OTP or bank details with anyone.

stories.title: BJP dominates UP voter preference on 256 of 403 seats:Samajwadi Party at 135; NDA allies may face maximum losses
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, a large-scale survey conducted by the Dainik Bhaskar app indicates a largely stable political landscape with limited shifts at the top. Across 403 Assembly constituencies, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) emerges as the first preference on 256 seats, while the Samajwadi Party (SP) leads on 135. The most notable losses are projected among BJP’s allies. The Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), led by Om Prakash Rajbhar, trails on all six of its current seats. Only SP shows gains in the survey A comparison with current seat holdings suggests marginal losses for the BJP and clear gains for the SP. The BJP, which currently holds 258 seats, is projected to fall short by two seats. In contrast, the SP, with 107 seats at present, is estimated to rise to 135 — a net gain of 28 seats. Other parties show either stagnation or decline. Regional trends: gains and losses For analysis, the state was divided into five regions — Purvanchal (133 seats), Awadh (82), Western UP (79), Braj (56), and Bundelkhand (53). The BJP registers gains in Purvanchal and Western Uttar Pradesh, while facing losses in Awadh, Braj, and Bundelkhand. The SP’s performance shows a complementary pattern. It loses ground in Western Uttar Pradesh but expands in Purvanchal, Awadh, Braj, and Bundelkhand. Ministers’ seats: BJP ahead The Council of Ministers comprises 54 members, including the Chief Minister, with 41 MLAs and 13 MLCs. In the survey, the BJP is the first preference on 32 of the 41 ministerial Assembly seats. The SP leads on eight, while BJP ally Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) leads on one. BJP leads on allies’ seats A notable finding is the BJP’s lead on all nine Assembly seats currently held by its allies. On four seats held by Apna Dal (Sonelal) — Bindki, Nanpara, Vishwanathganj, and Shohratgarh — the BJP is the preferred choice. Similarly, on three seats held by the RLD — Khatauli, Thanabhawan, and Siwalkhas — respondents favour the BJP. The trend extends to SBSP-held constituencies, including Mahadeva and Mau, where the BJP also leads. Mau is represented by Abbas Ansari. Opposition gains on NDA seats Of the 290 seats held by the NDA (257 BJP and 33 allies), the SP emerges as the first preference on 75 seats. Within BJP-held constituencies, the SP leads on 59 seats and the Indian National Congress on one. Conversely, the BJP leads on 47 of the SP’s current 105 seats, indicating direct competition between the two principal parties. Muslim-represented constituencies show split trend The Assembly currently has 31 Muslim MLAs — 27 from the SP, two from the RLD, and one each from Apna Dal (S) and SBSP. In these constituencies, the BJP leads on 15 seats, while the SP leads on 16. In several seats represented by Muslim MLAs, including Thanabhawan, Siwalkhas, and Mau, the BJP emerges as the first preference. On the Suar seat, earlier associated with Azam Khan and later won by Apna Dal (S), the SP leads in the survey. First-time MLAs: BJP ahead There are 137 first-time MLAs in the Assembly, including 74 from the BJP and 41 from the SP. The survey places the BJP ahead on 86 of these seats, followed by the SP on 46. Smaller parties register limited preference across the remaining constituencies. Women MLAs: limited change The Assembly has 51 women MLAs — 30 from the BJP, 15 from the SP, four from Apna Dal (S), and one each from the RLD and Congress. The survey indicates minimal change in these constituencies. The BJP leads on 31 seats, the SP on 18, while Apna Dal (S) and Congress lead on one seat each. For each Assembly constituency, the party receiving the highest share of responses was identified as the “first preference”. The findings reflect voter inclination at the time of the survey and not a projection of final results.

stories.title: Samajwadi Party's 300 units free electricity plan under scrutiny:Annual cost could reach ₹82,000 crore, exceeding combined allocations of UP’s top 10 govt depts
stories.summary: Electricity has become a major political flashpoint in Uttar Pradesh. While the government appears on the back foot over the smart meter issue, Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav has announced that his party will provide 300 units of free electricity if it comes to power. If implemented, the scheme—along with existing electricity subsidies—could place an estimated burden of around ₹82,000 crore annually on the state exchequer. This amount exceeds the combined annual budgets of the state’s top 10 departments. Understanding the cost calculations In Uttar Pradesh, electricity consumption between 150 and 300 units is billed at around ₹6.5 per unit. Including meter charges, fixed charges, fuel adjustment charges, and taxes, the effective cost rises to approximately ₹8.5 per unit. According to Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation data, the state currently has around 3.5 crore domestic electricity connections. Of these, nearly 70%—about 2.45 crore consumers—use an average of 300 units per month. Providing 300 units of free electricity to these consumers would cost the state approximately ₹6,240 crore per month, pushing the annual burden to around ₹75,000 crore. The Uttar Pradesh government had presented a budget of about ₹9.13 lakh crore for 2026–27. Of this, ₹6,823 crore was allocated for schemes such as providing 140 units of free electricity to farmers and subsidies for weavers. Combining existing schemes with the proposed free electricity plan for households would take the total expenditure beyond ₹82,000 crore—more than the annual budget of even the power department, which received around ₹66,000 crore this year. Policy concerns: NEP-2026 recommends phasing out free power The trend of free electricity began with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) during the 2015 Delhi Assembly elections, when it promised 200 units of free power and later implemented it. The scheme continues even after a change in government. Since then, several states have introduced similar schemes. Currently, Karnataka offers 200 units free, Bihar 125 units, and Jharkhand 200 units. Rajasthan provides 150 units free for households with solar panel installations. Additionally, states like Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, and Jammu Kashmir run subsidy or waiver schemes for farmers, weavers, and low-income households. However, the draft of the National Electricity Policy-2026 (NEP-2026), released by the Power Ministry in January 2026, recommends gradually phasing out free electricity schemes. Samajwadi Party’s stand: Government will bear the cost Former Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary and Samajwadi Party strategist Alok Ranjan stated that free electricity schemes are already operational in several states, including Punjab, which provides 300 units free. He said that in Uttar Pradesh, the burden of such a scheme would not fall on power companies but on the government, which would compensate them through subsidies. With the state budget exceeding ₹9 lakh crore, he argued that the expenditure could be managed. BJP’s response: Wait for the manifesto BJP spokesperson Avneesh Tyagi said the party has already fulfilled its promises of providing electricity and free utilities to farmers. He added that earlier, electricity supply was limited to only a few districts. Regarding the 2027 Assembly elections, he said there is still time, and any concessions would be detailed in the party’s manifesto based on public needs. Why electricity has become a political issue in UP Around 10 to 12 states across India currently offer some form of free electricity or subsidies. With Assembly elections due in Uttar Pradesh in about eight months, electricity has emerged as a key electoral issue. Public anger has been growing over electricity privatization and the rollout of smart prepaid meters. In an election year, even BJP MLAs and councillors have joined public protests. Responding to the backlash, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has formed a committee to investigate technical flaws in smart meters, with a report expected within 10 days. Until then, the replacement of old meters with smart meters has been halted, although new connections continue to receive smart prepaid meters. Amid this backdrop, Akhilesh Yadav’s promise of 300 units of free electricity has further intensified the political battle over power in the state.

stories.title: One school records 14 UP board toppers:5 Intermediate and 9 High School students make merit list
stories.summary: A school in Naubasta, Kanpur, has delivered an exceptional performance in the Uttar Pradesh Board examinations, setting a new record. A total of 14 students from the institution have secured places in the UP Board merit list—five from the Intermediate level and nine from High School. Paritosh Inter College alone contributed all 14 students to the merit list. Among them, Amit Sahu (Intermediate) and Disha Pandey (High School) emerged as city toppers, securing the first position in Kanpur in their respective categories. Focus on discipline and practice drives success School Principal Rachna Awasthi attributed this remarkable achievement to the consistent hard work of both students and teachers. She emphasized that the school maintains a disciplined academic environment throughout the year and encourages regular study habits. Teachers focus not only on subject knowledge but also on answer-writing techniques, guiding students on how to effectively present their responses in exams. Continuous practice sessions are conducted for board students to strengthen their preparation. Additionally, special extra classes are held every Sunday to provide further academic support and guidance. This structured approach has played a key role in delivering such outstanding results this year. Top high school performers from Kanpur All the above students are from Paritosh Inter College, Hanspuram, Naubasta, Kanpur, reflecting the institution’s strong academic foundation and commitment to excellence.

stories.title: 7 relatives of UP’s crorepati peon arrested:Includes two wives and in-laws, ₹8 crore fraud carried out in DIOS office
stories.summary: Pilibhit police on Friday took major action against millionaire peon Ilham-ur-Rahman Shamsi, who had three wives. Police have arrested his two wives Lubna and Azara Khan, sister-in-law Fatima, mother-in-law Nahid, relative Aafia Khan, and acquaintances Parveen Khatoon and Aashkara Parveen, who were involved in a multi-crore scam. Ilham's first wife, Arshi Khatoon, had already been sent to jail by the police. She is currently out of jail on bail. The accused peon was posted at Bisalpur Inter College, 40 km from the district headquarters. Eight years ago, he managed to get an attachment in the District Inspector of Schools (DIOS) office through connections. Then he also started looking after tasks like generating tokens for salary. He made his three wives, mother-in-law, sister-in-law, and other relatives teachers, clerks, and contractors. 8 crore 15 lakh transferred to the accounts of all seven During the investigation, police have so far found 53 such bank accounts into which the scam money was transferred. The 7 accused whom the police have arrested and sent to jail, had received 8 crore 15 lakh rupees in their accounts over 8 years. This amount was sent in the name of salary and for fake work done in the college. Police have frozen 5 crore 50 lakh rupees deposited in different bank accounts. How was Ilham's scam caught? In February 2026, the Bank of Baroda manager sent a letter to Pilibhit DM Gyanendra Singh. It stated that 1 crore 15 lakh rupees had been transferred from the Treasury Office to a private bank account. After this, the DM constituted a three-member inquiry committee. During the investigation, it was revealed that a game of showing fake teachers and sending money to private bank accounts had been going on from the DIOS office for about 8 years. Used to generate fake salary tokens During the investigation, the name of peon Ilham came forward as the mastermind. It was found that the peon of the DIOS office generated fake salary tokens and used the account numbers of his relatives, but showed other names. He transferred crores of rupees of government money to the accounts of his three wives, sister-in-law, and other relatives. All three wives did not know - Ilham was already married Police investigation revealed that the accused Ilham has three wives. All of them lived in different places. Ilham had transacted 1.15 crore rupees in the bank account of his first wife, Arshi, which led to the revelation of the entire scam. Meanwhile, the second wife, Ajara, stated during interrogation that she was unaware of her husband's other marriages. She said she didn't even know who he married first. The accused Ilham had obtained anticipatory bail from the High Court on March 30. Meet Ilham's three wives First- Arshi Khatoon was arrested by the police on February 19 and sent to jail. However, she got bail from the court on March 28. Second- Ajara Khan is a resident of Bulandshahr. However, she used to live in Civil Line, Aligarh. Third- Lubna is a resident of Jagat Mohalla, Ramsatti police station area of Sambhal. How much money was transferred to the accounts of all seven accused? Full recovery of government funds will be made ASP Vikram Dahiya stated - The investigation has revealed that a total of 8 crore 15 lakh rupees reached the accounts of these seven accused. Out of this, more than 5 crore rupees have already been frozen. The police are now conducting a thorough investigation of other people and suspicious accounts connected to this entire network, to ensure full recovery of government funds.

stories.title: Warning of major agitation in Gorakhpur:Strong protest by power employees against privatization; warns of intensified protest if decision not withdrawn
stories.summary: Electricity employees openly protested against the proposed privatization and clearly stated that if the decision is not withdrawn, a major agitation will be launched in Gorakhpur. At the call of the Electricity Employees Joint Struggle Committee, electricity employees, engineers, and other staff from across the state came together. Everyone opposed the privatization of Purvanchal and Dakshinanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation, saying that this decision is not right for both common people and employees. The employees said that the transfer of an essential service like electricity into private hands will have the greatest impact on common consumers. They say that this could make electricity expensive and services could also weaken, which will increase people's problems. Concerns about impact on services and complaints Electricity employees believe that after privatization, complaints will not be resolved in a timely manner, and the system will not remain as reliable as before. This could cause difficulties for people in both villages and cities. Employees also said that privatization will affect their jobs and rights. Working conditions may change, and the risk of unfair treatment of employees may also increase. Allegations of negligence against management Pushpendra Singh, convener of Sangharsh Samiti Gorakhpur, alleged that the management is not paying attention to the problems of employees, and they are being harassed. He said that the legitimate demands of employees are being continuously ignored, and proper dialogue is not taking place. He clearly stated that if the harassment of employees does not stop and the decision of privatization is not withdrawn, then electricity workers will start a large-scale movement and will not back down under any circumstances. Demand for immediate decision from Govt Committee officials demanded that the government should immediately stop the privatization process and find a solution should be found through dialogue with all parties, so that the general public and employees do not suffer. On May Day, electricity workers united and reiterated their resolve that they will continue their fight in the public interest and make every possible effort to keep the electricity system strong.

stories.title: Fly found in Mumbai doctor’s Vande Bharat breakfast:Wife vomits, passengers protest in train, ask who will be responsible if food kills
stories.summary: On Friday in Agra, a fly was found in the breakfast of a Mumbai doctor traveling on the Vande Bharat train. The doctor's wife ate it. After this, she started vomiting, causing a commotion on the train. People traveling on Vande Bharat questioned the railway's food. During this, people created a huge ruckus on the moving Vande Bharat. They demanded a refund from the railway. The doctor expressed his displeasure to railway officials over the phone. He said, 'Tell me what action you will take after an insect is found. If there is food poisoning, and someone loses their life, will the railway compensate? Who will be responsible for this?' The incident occurred around 7 AM when the Vande Bharat train was traveling from Agra to Prayagraj. Passengers have made a video of the entire incident and made it viral. See 3 pictures Now read the full case Mumbai-based pediatrician Dr. Kapil Patil had come to Uttar Pradesh with his family on a religious pilgrimage. After visiting Kashi Vishwanath, the family boarded the Vande Bharat Express (coach C1 of train number 20176) to go to Prayagraj. When breakfast was served to them at Agra Railway Station during the journey, a dead insect (fly) was found in the packet of French fries. Dr. Patil claims that his wife unknowingly consumed the contaminated breakfast, shortly after which she started complaining of food poisoning and her health deteriorated significantly. Doctor said - tampering with passengers' health Dr. Kapil Patil was very upset with this negligence in the train. Taking a dig at Railways' 'premium' services and claims of cleanliness, he said, passengers pay high fares in modern and high-speed trains like Vande Bharat so that they can get safe, clean and better facilities, but here passengers' health is being openly tampered with. He said - Does the railway charge 'premium' fees for this level of safety and catering? As soon as the complaint of the incident was received, senior railway officials and the catering department team became active. Who will be responsible if someone dies? Its video has also surfaced. In it, the doctor is expressing his displeasure to railway officials over the phone. He is saying, "Tell me what action you will take after the worm is found. If food poisoning occurs and someone dies, will the railway compensate? Who will be responsible for this?" Your catering person was talking about the money for breakfast. If we go to court, you will have to pay millions in compensation, we understand that much. Your helpline number is also not connecting. Upon reaching Prayagraj, medical assistance was provided to the family, and considering the seriousness of the matter, an immediate investigation was ordered. Officials have assured the victim family that the quality of food and the negligence of the catering vendor will be thoroughly investigated. Notice Issued to Contractor Sanjay Gautam, Public Relations Officer of Agra Railway Division, stated - The incident occurred in coach C-13. A fly was found in the passenger's food. An investigation into the matter has been initiated. Catering contracts in railways are awarded by IRCTC under an agreement. In this matter, 'appropriate action' is being taken by IRCTC. A notice is being issued to the contractor. The railway will take appropriate action as per rules.

stories.title: Justice timeline set after Maha Kumbh stampede:30-day deadline fixed, High Court action speeds process amid doubts on compensation and inquiry
stories.summary: When the chant of 'Har Har Gange' rises from millions of throats at the confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and the invisible Saraswati in Prayagraj, it is not merely a religious event; it is the pulsation of India's soul. Mahakumbh is a symbol of the unbroken faith of this country that has flowed for centuries, which did not waver with the rise and fall of kings, which was not broken by the swords of invaders. In the last Mahakumbh, the number of devotees broke all records. In such an event, many people lost their loved ones in the stampede on the night of Mauni Amavasya. Their pain is real, their tears are real. Both the government and the judiciary felt this pain. Where is the inconsistency in this? In the world of justice, one thing is repeatedly emphasised. Justice should not only be done, but it should also be seen to be done. And currently, this is what is happening in an open court, in front of everyone, with the complete process. After hearing the Mahakumbh stampede case, the Allahabad High Court gave clear instructions on April 30 - all compensation claims will be settled by the district administration within 30 days. The work of the judicial commission is only to investigate the causes of the stampede and to give suggestions for the future. Now, where is the inconsistency in this? Justice is not just being done, it is also being seen. Searching for Political Future in Pain When a major tragedy occurs, two types of people come forward. One, those who start healing the wounds, and the other, those who keep scratching the wounds. Not because they are concerned about the victims, but because they see their political future in this pain. Nevertheless, in light of the court's order, we try to find an answer to the question: Did the government ever back down from its responsibility? Did it turn away from its responsibility? Entrusting responsibility to the administration is correct Those who raise such questions actually do not understand the judicial process, or deliberately misrepresent it even after understanding it. That the district administration should decide the compensation, there is deep understanding in this. The district administration is the unit that is on the ground. Which knows the circumstances of every victim family. Which can tell which house's earner is gone, which family has small children, who has no other support. No remote committee, no commission sitting in Delhi or Lucknow, can make this sensitive assessment. That is why the court entrusted this responsibility to those who are closest. This is not administrative coldness, this is practical sensitivity. Not delay, but certainty Separating investigation from compensation is a fundamental principle of justice. If the same institution investigates and also determines compensation, it will not be justice, but a monopoly of power. Investigation separate, compensation separate, so that there is transparency, accountability, and no one gets a chance to complain. Now, let's talk about the 30-day deadline. Some people will call this a delay, but it is not a delay, it is certainty. The High Court has eliminated uncertainty by setting a deadline. Now a clear clock is ticking. There is a binding deadline. There is a fixed date by which everyone will have received compensation. This is the work that a responsible, sensitive, and active judiciary does. In any accident, verifying claims, and collecting facts and documents takes time. Therefore, this deadline given to the district administration is a process to establish solid and sustainable accountability. Commission to bring out the truth Now let's go back to that night of the 2025 Mahakumbh, when the accident happened. We need to see what the government did. Immediate relief and rescue operations began. The injured were taken to the hospital. Affected families were contacted. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath himself monitored the situation. And most importantly... the formation of an independent judicial commission. Why was this commission formed? Not to hide the truth, but so that the truth comes out completely, impartially, and without any pressure. When you declare a commission 'ineffective' even before its report is out, you are not demanding justice; you are pre-determining the conclusion. If someone calls a 30-day deadline 'delay', assume that they either do not understand the judicial process or do not want to understand it for vested reasons. Responsibility with Sensitivity Accidents have happened in Mahakumbh before as well. Who can forget the accident that occurred at Allahabad station during the 2013 Mahakumbh, which happened on the day of Mauni Amavasya itself? However, there is a difference in sensitivity and responsibility between the incident of that time and the incident of 2025. The Yogi government understood its responsibility seriously. The Sangam is still there today. Just like the streams of Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati flowing in it, the streams of the judiciary, administration, and government are also flowing in one direction. In the direction of justice. In the direction of truth. In the direction of the rights of the victims. The path to justice is not easy. But when the system is walking on that path, with honesty, accountability, and transparency, we should trust it, because trust is the foundation upon which the palace of justice stands.

stories.title: Mahamandaleshwar cheats widow of ₹10 lakh and jewellery:At Ghaziabad flat, took ornaments off her, handed fake government job letter to son
stories.summary: A religious leader from Ghaziabad swindled 10.5 lakh rupees and gold jewelry from a widow residing in Ambala, Haryana. The woman alleges that the religious leader, Mahamandaleshwar Yogi Anand Giri Maharaj, lured her with the promise of a job in the central government. The accused also handed over a fake joining letter to her son. They called him to Delhi multiple times for joining. When the job didn't materialize, the religious leader and his accomplice absconded. The religious leader Anand Giri used to introduce himself as the founder of the Human Rights Protection Association. After this, he also made the victim the president of the association's women's wing in Haryana, to gain her trust. Know How trust was gained and fraud committed, according to the FIR Came to blood donation camp, stayed at home According to Sunita, a resident of Kala Amb, Ambala, a blood donation camp was held in Kala Amb on December 21, 2025. Anand Giri and his associate Manish Mishra were the chief guests. To attend the camp, both stayed at the woman's house on December 20. Anand Giri had told Sunita that one of his disciples held a high government post in Delhi. Deception to get son appointed as ASO According to Sunita, Anand Giri said that he could directly get her younger son, Rishabh Bansal, appointed to the post of ASO (Assistant Section Officer) in the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions without an examination. In return, it would cost 10 lakh rupees. I immediately gave him 50 thousand rupees as an advance. After that, I borrowed 5 lakh rupees and transferred them to Anand Giri's bank account on December 29, 2025. Subsequently, another 5 lakh rupees were transferred. Fake Joining Letter Given Sunita stated that on January 16, 2026, Anand Giri called her and her son Rishabh to his flat in Ghaziabad. There, he gave them a joining letter in a sealed envelope, which appeared completely government-issued upon reading. His associate Manish got them to sign a blank form and said that after getting it attested by an IAS officer, the joining would be done by January 19. Woman's jewelry was taken off Sunita further stated, even after January 19, the joining did not happen, and the accused started procrastinating. In March, the accused called me to Delhi. After this, Anand Giri's phone started coming up as switched off. When I reached the flat in Ghaziabad, Anand Giri said that the officers were demanding 5 lakh rupees more. As there was no money, Anand Giri had the gold ring, chain, and earrings removed and said that the joining would happen tomorrow. Fake Aadhaar card exposed the truth, now received threats According to Sunita, when her son's joining didn't happen for a long time, I went back to the Ghaziabad flat, where it was found that both accused have been absconding since March 16. A fake Aadhaar card of Anand Giri was also found there. The woman said, when asked for money, Anand Giri threatened her. He said- You have only a few people, I have the support of millions, you cannot harm me.Anand Giri's file photo.Read in 2 points, what the police investigation foundFraud in the name of job: The woman's complaint was sent to the Economic Offence Wing (EOW) Ambala for investigation. The investigation found the complaint to be true. The investigation revealed that the accused Anand Giri alias Anand Pandit and Manish Mishra defrauded ?10.50 lakh and jewelry in the name of government jobs and provided a fake appointment letter.Case registered under several sections: Police have registered case number 155 against both accused under sections 316(2), 318(4), 338, 336(3), 340(2) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at Narayangarh police station and started investigation.SHO said - Case registered against Mahamandaleshwar and associateNarayanagarh Police Station SHO Lalit Kumar said that based on the woman's complaint, the police have registered a case against Mahamandaleshwar Yogi Anand Giri Maharaj and his associate Manish Mishra. Police are thoroughly investigating the matter. Further action will be taken based on the investigation.Anand Giri and associate's mobile switched offWhen Dainik Bhaskar reporter tried to contact Anand Giri and his associate, their mobile number was found switched off. Another number registered in the FIR was also called, where the person who received the call identified himself as an LIC officer. No response was received even after messaging on WhatsApp.

stories.title: Businessman jumps from 11th floor after calling wife:Says he lost everything in IPL, had married for love 8 months ago
stories.summary: A 35-year-old property dealer in Lucknow committed suicide by jumping from the 11th floor. He used to bet on IPL matches. On Thursday, he lost millions of rupees in the match between RCB and Gujarat Giants. After this, he called his wife. Crying, he said - I have lost everything. His wife tried to console him, but he jumped from the apartment's balcony during the match. Hearing the sound of the young man falling, people from the society rushed there, but by then the young man had already died. Police, who arrived on receiving the information, found a suicide note at the scene, in which Prabal had written about losing money in the match. Prabal Jain, a resident of Sitapur, lived on rent in Janeshwar Apartment in the Gudamba police station area. He had a love marriage just 8 months ago. At the time of the incident, his wife was in Sitapur. They were talking on the phone. The incident happened on Thursday night at 8:30 PM. At that time, the match between RCB and Gujarat Giants was going on. People were strolling outside, running to hear the sound of the fall On Thursday night around 8:30 PM, Prabal jumped from the 11th floor. The weather was pleasant after the rain, and people were walking around in the society. Hearing the sound of him falling, people rushed there. A crowd gathered. Cries erupted at the scene. People present there informed the ambulance and the police. The police, who arrived at the scene, took Prabal to the hospital. There, doctors declared him dead. ACP Ghaziabad Anindya Vikram Singh said that a suicide note was also found at the spot. It stated that he lost money in the match. He apologized to his wife and family. An investigation will be conducted based on the bank statement and the family's complaint. Wife said - He called me crying Wife Shivani stated during interrogation - He always used to watch IPL. Last night too, he was watching the match. During that time, he called me. He was crying a lot. He only told me that he had lost a lot. After that, he couldn't say anything and the call disconnected. Love happened during studies, then they got married Prabal Jain and Shivani, a resident of Bokaro, Jharkhand, met during their studies at Integral University. They had an affair and got married. Residents of Janeshwar Apartment said - both had come to live here last year during Diwali and did not socialise much with people. The deceased's father had also committed suicide some time ago, while his mother had also passed away. In session betting, bookies place bets on the runs or wickets scored in every ball, over, or session (10-15 overs). Prabal had lost a lot of money in session betting.

stories.title: UP Congress chief Ajay Rai falls ill, hospitalised in Lucknow:Faints at party event; admitted to Medanta Hospital
stories.summary: UP Congress president Ajay Rai’s health suddenly worsened on Friday afternoon. He fainted and was immediately admitted to Medanta Hospital, where he was treated under the supervision of expert doctors in the emergency ward. Tests were conducted to check for a possible brain stroke or heart attack. A team of doctors is closely monitoring his condition. At the time his health deteriorated, Ajay Rai was attending an event at the party headquarters. He suddenly complained of uneasiness and chest pain. He decided to return home, but lost consciousness on the way. Chest pain at the state office In Lucknow, the Congress organised a conference for teachers and doctors on Friday to mark Labour Day and Buddha Purnima. Several leaders, including Avinash Pandey and Supriya Shrinate from Delhi, attended the event. Ajay Rai had gone to drop UP in-charge Avinash Pandey at the airport after the programme. He then returned to the party office on Mall Avenue, where another event was underway. It was here that his health worsened and he experienced chest pain. He told his colleagues he was feeling anxious and asked to be taken home. He was being taken to his apartment in Telibagh, but his condition worsened on the way. He was immediately rushed to Medanta Hospital. Blood samples were taken to check for a heart attack Dr Rakesh Kapoor, Director of Medanta Lucknow, said Ajay Rai was brought in after his sudden health issue. He was admitted to the emergency ward with complaints of chest pain, uneasiness and unconsciousness. Treatment began under expert supervision, and specialists from multiple departments were deployed. After being admitted, his blood samples were sent for tests. Troponin T and Troponin I tests were also conducted, and both came back normal. A cardiologist and the ICU head are currently present. Fainted due to low sodium levels According to doctors, Ajay Rai felt unconscious due to low sodium levels. Initially, a stroke was suspected, and a CT scan of the brain was conducted. At present, there is no serious concern. He has been shifted to the Critical Care Medicine department and has regained consciousness.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Voters flag bad conduct, poor performance of UP MLAs; EC to hold repoll at Bengal's 15 booths tomorrow more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Govt hikes commercial LPG 5 kg cylinder prices From 1 May, 2026, several important financial changes may affect the daily lives of common man. These updates range from changes in commercial LPG cylinder prices to new online gaming laws. 2. Voters flag bad conduct, poor performance of UP MLAs in Bhaskar Survey In the biggest-ever Dainik Bhaskar survey, people rated the behaviour of 62 MLAs as poor. Among them were four women MLAs and four ministers. In Uttar Pradesh, the biggest factor behind public approval or disapproval was development work. Out of 400 MLAs, 281 were disliked by people for failing to deliver development in their constituencies. 3. OP Rajbhar loses cool at SP MLA, says, ‘I’ll smash you’ A non-bailable warrant has been issued by a Mau court against OP Rajbhar, who had once said, “If BJP leaders come asking for votes, beat them with shoes.” Rajbhar made the remark during the 2019 Lok Sabha election campaign. 4. EC to hold repoll at Bengal's 15 booths tomorrow The Election Commission of India has ordered re-polling in 15 polling stations in South 24 Parganas for the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections, following reports from Returning Officers and election observers. 5. Rapist gets 20 years' imprisonment, had assaulted an 8-year-old girl In Gorakhpur, Deendayal Nishad, a resident of Kusuli village in the Chauri Chaura police station area, has been sentenced to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for raping a minor girl. Special POCSO Judge Shamim Ahmad Ansari, while delivering the verdict, also imposed a fine of ₹25,000 on the convict. 6. 26-year-old woman’s throat slit inside Meerut home in front of 3 kids A 26-year-old woman was found murdered with her throat slit at her home in Meerut on Friday morning. The incident took place in Gali No. 3 of Majid Nagar under Lisari Gate police station limits, where Kausar, wife of Saqib, was found lying dead near the bed inside a room. 7. 'You'll be on the floor,' Heinrich Klaasen warns the fan In a viral video on social media, Klaasen was seen asking the fan not to take pictures of him and his family. He threatened the fan with severe consequences. 8. Moradabad molestation accused shot in an encounter A 45-year-old cleric, identified as the man accused of molesting a burqa-clad woman in a deserted lane in Moradabad, has turned out to be a ladies’ tailor. Police shot him in the leg during an encounter. He sustained a bullet injury in his left leg. 9. Ajay Pal Sharma lands in fresh row: Warns TMC candidate in WB IPS officer Ajay Pal Sharma is once again in the spotlight after landing in controversy over allegedly threatening an All India Trinamool Congress candidate while serving as an election observer in West Bengal. 10. Iran sends new proposal for US talks via Pakistan Iran has delivered a new proposal for talks with the United States via mediator Pakistan, state news agency IRNA reported on Friday. "The Islamic Republic of Iran delivered the text of its latest negotiating proposal to Pakistan, as the mediator in talks with the United States, on Thursday evening," the official IRNA news agency reported, without elaborating.

stories.title: CCTV footage exposes how Jeetu Saini shot 3 friends:Birthday cake argument turned violent; accused returned with weapons and opened fire inside gym
stories.summary: Jeetu Saini, who murdered three friends in Khurja, Bulandshahr, has been killed in an encounter. After his death, a major revelation has been made regarding the murder. Jeetu, a bodybuilder who was Mr. UP, cut a cake at the gym and left from there. Then he returned with friends and fired about 50 rounds in approximately 3 minutes. He shot and killed three friends. All this has been captured in the CCTV's DVR (Digital Video Recorder), which is with the police. The approximately 10-minute recording contains the complete story of the three murders. Who fired first, what were both brothers and the nephew of the BJP leader doing in their final moments? To know this, a 'Dainik Bhaskar' reporter spoke to police personnel. Read what has happened sequentially so far? First, know what is in the CCTV DVR? Police recovered the DVR from Mayank Saini, a friend of the main accused, Jeetu Saini. According to police sources, BJP councillor Sanjay Saini's brother Manish (30), nephew Akash (19), and cousin Amardeep (32) were sitting on chairs inside the gym at night. Amardeep was drinking something from a can. During this, 10 to 12 youths including Jeetu Saini, Mayank Saini, Bharat Saini, Rinku Saini, Rupesh Saini arrived. Jeetu Saini and two of his other associates had pistols in their hands, while two others had country-made pistols. Jeetu cocked the pistol below the gym, then entered the gym after firing a shot in the air towards the road. As soon as they entered, Jeetu and Amardeep came face to face. A conversation took place between the two for about 10 seconds. Then Jeetu fired three to four rounds at Amardeep with his pistol. Seeing the firing, his cousin Manish and nephew Akash both ran to save their lives. Everyone started running helter-skelter, and Jeetu began firing indiscriminately. After shooting Amardeep, when Jeetu advanced towards Manish, the second accused shot Manish in the head, and when he fell, fired three to four rounds at his body. After this, all of them together advanced towards Akash, firing indiscriminately, and shot him as well. Throughout this entire incident, Jeetu's friend, Rupesh (gym owner), repeatedly tried to stop him. He kept saying - Brother, don't hit them, let them go... leave them. But Jeetu and his friends kept firing until the magazine was empty. Approximately 50 rounds were fired in 3 minutes. After committing this murder, Jeetu also pointed a pistol at Rupesh's head. He threatened to kill him too and took the DVR of the CCTV cameras with him after having it opened. He knew that the entire video of the murder had been captured in the DVR. What was the real reason for the murder? Former BSP city president Jeetu Saini's birthday was on April 26. Before this, two parties were organised on April 25. One in a gym, the other party at Mayank Saini's pottery factory. Amardeep Saini, Manish Saini, and Akash Saini arrived at Rupesh Saini's RJS Fitness Gym between 910 PM with a birthday cake. There, they had all gathered to celebrate Jeetu Saini's birthday. Meanwhile, Jeetu was celebrating his birthday party at his friend Mayank Saini's pottery factory, 300 meters away from the gym. Amardeep called Jeetu and invited him to the gym. The cake was cut here. It was then that a dispute arose over applying cake to the face. A heated argument ensued between Jeetu's friend, Mayank Saini and Amardeep, Manish, and Akash. From here, Jeetu went back to Mayank's pottery factory with his friends. Everyone drank alcohol again here. Around 11 PM, Amardeep called Mayank. An argument ensued between the two. The next day, April 26, he had also said something regarding the 'terahvin' ceremony to be held at Mayank's house. Jeetu was also listening to this conversation on Mayank's phone, when both of them, enraged, reached the gym with three weapons along with other companions, and Jeetu fired indiscriminately, first shooting Amardeep, then Manish, and finally Akash in the head, killing them. However, apart from the dispute over the cake and the story of three murders, the police are also investigating other angles. Jeetu Saini had made a reel at Mayank's factory on April 25 Jeetu Saini had hosted a liquor party at Mayank Saini's pottery factory on April 25, where a reel was made. The background music in this reel was also set to: ‘I will kill you... I will kill you... I will definitely kill you, you better find a way to save yourself...’ Police action so far: Jeetu Saini killed, three injured in 'half encounter' Based on the complaint filed by Amardeep's father Sarup Saini, the police registered a murder case against Jeetu Saini, Jeetu's brother Ravi Saini, Mayank Saini, Mayank's brother Rinku Saini, Naresh alias Deva, Bharat Saini, Manish, gym owner Roopa alias Rupesh, Anuj, and Saurabh alias Seetu. After the incident, DIG Kalanidhi Naithani inspected the site and formed eight teams to search for the accused and investigate the case. The next day, on April 26, ADG Bhanu Bhaskar inspected the crime scene and spoke to the family members. Police have so far arrested three accused, Mayank, Rinku, and Bharat, in a half-encounter in this case. Rupesh and Naresh were arrested by the police from Khurja. Additionally, four police teams are continuously searching for the four absconding accused in Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, and Uttarakhand. The main accused in the murder, birthday boy Jeetu Saini (30), was killed by the police in an encounter five days after the incident. Inspector Mohd. Aslam and Head Constable Mohit Malik were injured in the encounter. Both have been admitted to a higher centre. Additionally, two constables, Ramphal and Kapil, were shot in their bulletproof jackets. -

stories.title: Agra women remove and dump smart meters:Hundreds reach electricity office carrying them on heads; say this is unacceptable
stories.summary: Women staged a protest against smart meters in Agra on Friday morning. Around 10 AM, a large number of women marched from the Devi Temple in Akola town to a nearby feeder, carrying smart meters on their heads and later throwing them on the ground in protest. People also brought smart meters in sacks and dumped them at the site. After this, the women and villagers sat on a protest and raised strong slogans against the electricity department. The women said they could not tolerate smart meters, while villagers demanded that the system be stopped immediately and that irregularities in electricity bills be investigated. See 2 pictures Villagers said - electricity bills are increasing with smart meters Villagers say that installing smart meters is increasing electricity bills and putting a burden on their financial situation. They have demanded that old meters be kept and the electricity department resolve their problems. The protest was led by Lavania, district president of Bharatiya Kisan Union (Tikait).

stories.title: Farmer dies after crop damage in rain:8 UP districts hit; groom’s car stuck; 17 deaths reported in 36 hours
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh has been facing bad weather for the last three days, with rain, strong winds and storms affecting many districts. At least 17 people have died in the past 36 hours due to storm-related incidents, while a sharp drop in temperature has brought relief from the heatwave. Rain has been falling in Gorakhpur since Friday morning, and most cities across the state remain under cloudy skies. Strong winds are blowing, and although no official rain alert has been issued for today, the Meteorological Department has warned of storms and lightning in 62 districts. Wind speeds may reach between 40 and 60 km per hour. The state has recorded an average rainfall of 2.6 mm during this period. The sudden change in weather has reduced temperatures by 10 to 12 degrees Celsius. Banda, which was the world’s hottest city just two days ago at 47.6°C, has now cooled down to 36.4°C. On Thursday, heavy hailstorms were reported in Ghaziabad, Noida, Lalitpur, Agra and Mathura, while more than 20 districts received rainfall. Jalaun recorded the highest temperature in the state that day at 43.6°C. Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- The effect of the cyclonic system formed around Northern Pakistan and Jammu and Kashmir has now ended. A new western disturbance may become active in the western Himalayan regions from May 2. This will change the weather in the hilly areas. Its effect will also be seen in UP. Here, there may be rain with thunder and lightning. How will the weather be for the next 5 days?

stories.title: Moradabad molestation accused shot in encounter:45-year-old ladies’ tailor hit in leg; accused of molesting a burqa-clad woman
stories.summary: A 45-year-old cleric, identified as the man accused of molesting a burqa-clad woman in a deserted lane in Moradabad, has turned out to be a ladies’ tailor. Police shot him in the leg during an encounter. He sustained a bullet injury in his left leg. The encounter took place near Jama Masjid in the city at around 11 pm on Thursday. Police said that when they surrounded the accused, he opened fire. In retaliatory firing, a bullet hit his left leg. He is currently undergoing treatment at the district hospital. Two days earlier, on 29 April, Naushad allegedly followed the woman, caught hold of her and behaved obscenely with her. He fled after the woman raised an alarm. On Thursday, after CCTV footage of the incident surfaced, police identified Naushad. Five police teams had been deployed to trace him. According to police, Naushad is unmarried. Investigation has revealed that he had allegedly behaved indecently with several women in the past as well. However, no woman had filed a complaint against him earlier. Accused admitted to hospital after being shot in encounter SP City Ran Vijay Singh said that on Wednesday, Naushad had publicly misbehaved with a woman in the Mughalpura police station area. His act was captured on CCTV footage, which helped police identify him. He is a resident of Pirzada Maqbara in Katghar. Five police teams were searching for Naushad. At around 10 pm on Thursday, police received information that he was present near Jama Masjid on the banks of the Ramganga river in the Mughalpura police station area. Acting on the tip-off, police teams cordoned off the entire area. Police asked Naushad to surrender, but he allegedly opened fire at them. In retaliatory firing, he was injured and fell to the ground. Police then overpowered him. A country-made pistol and three cartridges were recovered from his possession. Police have also traced the woman who was targeted in the molestation case. Based on her complaint, an FIR has been registered against the accused. Victim says accused fled after she screamed According to the victim, she was on her way for work on Wednesday afternoon when a man began molesting her. “He ran away when I screamed,” she said. In the CCTV footage, the woman is seen walking through a lane wearing a burqa and carrying a bag in her hand. Naushad can be seen following her quietly from behind for some distance. He then suddenly approaches the woman, grabs her and behaves obscenely. As soon as the woman screams, the accused starts running away. The woman chases him for some distance, shouting loudly, but Naushad manages to escape.

stories.title: 26-year-old woman’s throat slit inside Meerut home before 3 children:Husband left an hour earlier; daughter speaks of ‘black-clad intruder’
stories.summary: A 26-year-old woman was found murdered with her throat slit at her home in Meerut on Friday morning. The incident took place in Gali No. 3 of Majid Nagar under Lisari Gate police station limits, where Kausar, wife of Saqib, was found lying dead near the bed inside a room. At the time the body was discovered, her husband was not at home. He had left around an hour earlier on his e-rickshaw for work at the mandi. Kausar was in the room with her three young daughters. The incident is believed to have taken place between 6 am and 6.30 am. The body was first seen by the landlord’s wife, who immediately informed her husband, Israr. He then alerted Kausar’s husband, the police and neighbours. Police reached the spot and began an investigation. Landlord's wife discovered the body Landlord’s wife first spotted the body Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, landlord Israr alias Sonu said that around 8 am, Saqib’s children came downstairs and asked his wife to call their father. The children were very young and only asked for their father to be called, without explaining why. Israr called Saqib from his mobile phone and handed the phone to the children, who took it upstairs. While speaking to their father, the children suddenly began crying loudly. Sensing something was wrong, Israr asked his wife to go upstairs and check. When she entered the room, she was shocked. She screamed loudly, and Israr rushed upstairs. He found Kausar’s body lying on the floor near the bed in a pool of blood, with her throat slit. He told his wife not to touch anything as it had become a police case. They then informed Saqib, called police and alerted neighbours. Israr said he had no idea how the murder took place, as his family was asleep downstairs and heard no screams, commotion or disturbance. “Had there been any noise, we would have rushed up immediately,” he said. Husband had left home about an hour earlier According to Saqib, he lived on rent on the second floor of a two-storey house owned by Sonu, son of Qadeer, in Majid Nagar. He lived there with his wife Kausar and their three daughters. He said he had left early in the morning to drive his rickshaw. Shortly after, landlord Sonu called him and informed him that his wife had been murdered and her body was lying in the room with her throat slit, the room soaked in blood. Saqib rushed home in his rickshaw and found a crowd gathered outside. When he entered, he saw his wife’s body lying inside the room. He said he had left his wife and daughters asleep, only to return and find her dead. The sight left him devastated. Kausar was 26 years old and originally from Loni. She had married Saqib around seven years ago. Blood stains found up to the courtyard After news of the murder spread, neighbours gathered at the house. Blood stains were seen from the room to the courtyard and even up to the roof area. The entire room was covered in blood. Landlord Israr, who works on mobile towers, was at home along with his wife Farah and their three children. Daughter says ‘a man in black clothes came’ Saqib said his eldest daughter is Saniya, followed by Kulsuminar, and a third younger daughter. One of the girls told family members that “a thief wearing black clothes” had entered their room. She said their father was not at home, and the man used a stone to climb up and enter the house. He caught hold of her mother, killed her and fled. At the time, the other two sisters were asleep.

stories.title: 16-year-old climbs high-tension electricity pole in Gorakhpur:Demands to live with boyfriend; police coax her down via WhatsApp after 2.5-hour standoff
stories.summary: A 16-year-old girl in Gorakhpur’s Chiluatal area climbed a high-tension electricity pole while insisting on living at her boyfriend’s house, triggering panic in the area. Hundreds gathered at the spot as onlookers began recording videos on their mobile phones. After receiving information, Chiluatal police reached the spot and began efforts to bring the girl down safely. Following nearly two-and-a-half hours of intense efforts, police sent her a WhatsApp message assuring her that her condition would be considered. Only after reading the message did she agree to climb down. Now know the complete matter The teenager, a resident of the Chiluatal area, had gone missing from home a month ago. On her mother’s complaint, police registered a kidnapping case, recovered the girl, and arrested Shivam alias Ganesh, a resident of Balapar, sending him to jail. After completing legal formalities, the girl was sent home with her mother. On Thursday morning around 9 am, she climbed a high-tension pole near the Kolhua Ghat concrete bridge. Police tried to persuade her to come down, but initial efforts failed. Message sent on mobile phone When police contacted her on mobile, she remained adamant about living at her boyfriend’s house. Following this, a settlement agreement was prepared with the boyfriend and sent to her on WhatsApp. After reading the message, she climbed down safely. SP North Gyanendra Kumar said a teenage girl had climbed a high-tension electricity pole and was safely brought down after counselling. He said she has been sent home with her mother, and police will continue counselling her further.

stories.title: Rapist sentenced to 20 years in jail:Accused assaulted 8-year-old girl in sugarcane field; victim gets justice after 6 years
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, Deendayal Nishad, a resident of Kusuli village in the Chauri Chaura police station area, has been sentenced to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for raping a minor girl. Special POCSO Judge Shamim Ahmad Ansari, while delivering the verdict, also imposed a fine of ₹25,000 on the convict. If the fine is not paid, accused Deendayal will have to serve an additional two years in prison. After the verdict was delivered on Thursday, the victim’s family broke down in tears. Her relatives said, “He ruined our child’s life.” Justice after 6 years Special Public Prosecutor Rammilan Singh, appearing for the victim’s side, said the incident took place at around 8 pm on July 2, 2020. The complainant’s eight-year-old daughter had gone with two village children to a nearby area to pluck neem leaves. When they could not find neem leaves, the two children returned home, but the girl was left behind. On the way, she was allegedly intercepted by accused Deendayal Nishad at a deserted spot. Seeing her alone, he covered her mouth and carried her to a sugarcane field, where he allegedly assaulted her in the darkness of night before fleeing, leaving the child severely injured. When the girl did not return home for a long time, her family began searching for her and found her unconscious in the sugarcane field. She was rushed to hospital for treatment. Her mother later lodged a complaint at Chauri Chaura police station, following which a case was registered. The court has now delivered its verdict in the case after 6 years.

stories.title: Voters flag bad conduct, poor performance of UP lawmakers:58 MLAs, 4 ministers draw flak over errant behaviour
stories.summary: In the biggest-ever Dainik Bhaskar survey, people rated the behaviour of 62 MLAs as poor. Among them were four women MLAs and four ministers. In Uttar Pradesh, the biggest factor behind public approval or disapproval was development work. Out of 400 MLAs, 281 were disliked by people for failing to deliver development in their constituencies. There were also eight MLAs on whom voters could not form a clear opinion. These included five from Bharatiya Janata Party, one from Samajwadi Party and two from Nishad Party. We understand survey results in 2 ways- Public opinion on women MLAs 41 disliked for lack of development Uttar Pradesh Assembly has 51 women MLAs. Of them, 30 belong to the Bharatiya Janata Party, 15 to the Samajwadi Party, four to Apna Dal (Sonelal), and one each from Rashtriya Lok Dal and Indian National Congress. In the survey, people rated the work of 41 women MLAs as poor. This included 26 from the BJP, 11 from the SP, three from Apna Dal (S), and one from the RLD. Four women MLAs were rejected by people due to poor behaviour — three from the BJP and one from the SP. Six women MLAs were liked for their good behaviour. Among them, three were from the SP, while one each belonged to the BJP, Apna Dal (S) and Congress. Public Opinion on Ministers 30 out of 39 ministers unhappy over not getting development work done The Uttar Pradesh government has 54 ministers, including 14 MLCs and 40 MLAs, with Yogi Adityanath among them. The Bhaskar survey found that, excluding the Chief Minister, people were unhappy with 30 out of 39 ministers for not delivering development work. These 30 included 11 Cabinet ministers, eight Ministers of State (Independent Charge), and 11 Ministers of State.
