stories.title: IPS Ajay Pal Sharma sparks fresh row:Warns TMC candidate during election duty in WB; a look at his past disputes
stories.summary: IPS officer Ajay Pal Sharma is once again in the spotlight after landing in controversy over allegedly threatening a All India Trinamool Congress candidate while serving as an election observer in West Bengal. The controversy has united the Opposition against him. Akhilesh Yadav said such officers would be tracked down and punished when the time comes. The TMC, meanwhile, has threatened action against Ajay after the elections. But this is not the first time Ajay Pal Sharma has been surrounded by controversy. He has previously faced allegations of corruption, destruction of evidence and intimidation. Let's understand the complete story from the beginning... Had registered a chicken theft case against Azam Khan As Superintendent of Police, Ajay Pal Sharma got his first posting during the Samajwadi Party government. In February 2016, he was appointed SP of Hathras. About eight months later, in October, he was shifted to Shamli district. After Yogi Adityanath’s government came to power in 2017, Ajay Pal Sharma carried out a series of encounters. He was then given charge of Noida — and that is where the controversies began and have continued ever since. He faced allegations of taking an Rs 80 lakh bribe from a call centre operator. Several encounters came under scrutiny. A woman journalist accused him of framing her in a false case and cheating her. The complaint eventually reached Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Following this, during a video conference, the Chief Minister reportedly reprimanded Ajay strongly. A few days later, he was removed from Noida and transferred to Rampur. While serving as Rampur SP, cases of chicken theft, goat theft and robbery of Rs 10,000 were registered against senior SP leader Azam Khan and his wife Tanzeen Fatima. Senior made allegations of money exchange in transfer-posting In January 2020, while posted in Rampur, Ajay Pal Sharma faced a major corruption allegation. Then SSP of Noida, Vaibhav Krishna, sent a report to the Chief Minister and DGP accusing Ajay Pal Sharma and five IPS officers of taking money in exchange for transfer and posting deals. Apart from Ajay, the report named Himanshu Kumar, Ganesh Saha, Rajeev Narayan Mishra and Sudhir Kumar Singh. They were accused of striking deals for prime postings, with evidence also submitted. After this, both Vaibhav Krishna and Ajay Pal Sharma were removed from their districts. Ajay was briefly attached to DGP Headquarters before being posted to the Police Training Centre in Unnao. Woman claimed to be his wife The Uttar Pradesh government formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the matter. Preliminary findings reportedly found merit in the allegations, after which an FIR was registered against Ajay Pal Sharma at the vigilance police station in Meerut. Around the same time, lawyer Deepti Sharma claimed she was Ajay Pal Sharma’s wife. She alleged that Ajay had entered into a registered marriage with her in 2016, but their relationship later deteriorated. She claimed that after a phone dispute in 2019, policemen from Rampur came to her home in Ghaziabad in September 2019 and took away a laptop and digital video recorder (DVR). She said she complained to the DIG of Meerut Range, but was later arrested. According to her, while she was in jail, multiple cases including cheating and charges under the IT Act were filed against her. Seeking a probe, she approached then Special Secretary (Home) Dr Anil Kumar Singh. Acting on his directions, a case was registered in March 2020 at Hazratganj police station in Lucknow against Ajay Pal Sharma and others under sections related to embezzlement, criminal conspiracy and destruction of evidence. A separate SIT was formed to investigate. Now know what happened in these cases... 1. Cash for Posting Case In February 2023, a court gave Ajay Pal Sharma a clean chit based on the SIT’s closure report. The report said no concrete evidence or witness was found to support allegations of money being exchanged for transfers and postings. His assets and bank accounts were also examined, and no disproportionate wealth was found. 2. Deepti Sharma Marriage Case Initially, two separate SITs investigated the allegations, but later the probes became linked due to overlap in facts. Based on the February 2023 closure report, Ajay also got a clean chit in the criminal conspiracy and destruction of evidence case. In the marriage-related allegations, Deepti Sharma’s claims and registration papers did not match government records. The marriage registrar stated in writing that no such marriage had ever been registered in that office. Forensic and technical investigations also found no evidence of tampering with records or digital evidence. Now know what happened in West Bengal Raid conducted at TMC candidate's house, video went viral Ajay Pal Sharma has been posted as an election observer in West Bengal and given charge of North 24 Parganas district, considered a stronghold of Abhishek Banerjee, nephew of Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. Ahead of the second phase of polling, TMC candidate Jahangir Khan from Falta seat was accused of intimidating voters and snatching ID cards. On 27 April, Ajay, accompanied by the Central Reserve Police Force, raided Jahangir’s house. Jahangir was not present. During the visit, Ajay was heard warning supporters that anyone involved in wrongdoing would be “dealt with properly”, and that if reports of intimidation continued, strict action would follow. The video of the raid quickly went viral. Posts by Akhilesh Yadav and Mahua Moitra The same day, Akhilesh Yadav shared the video on X, alleging that BJP had sent its “tested agents” in the name of observers, but said they would achieve nothing and face deep scrutiny and strict punishment at the right time. The next day, on 28 April, TMC MP Mahua Moitra shared two videos claiming Ajay was seen dancing with bar performers. Referring to him sarcastically as “Fair and Lovely Babua”, she posted in English that it was amusing to see him enjoying himself in “Fantacop style”. Later the same day, TMC moved the Calcutta High Court seeking Ajay Pal Sharma’s removal, accusing him of violating the Model Code of Conduct. The court, after an urgent hearing, said it would not pass any order against any officer deployed on election duty until 29 April — the date of second-phase polling. After the High Court’s decision, TMC filed an e-petition late at night in the Supreme Court of India. The matter is yet to be heard. Meanwhile, second-phase voting in West Bengal has already been completed on 29 April.

stories.title: 60 kmph winds, heavy rain lash Lucknow:Power cuts hit city, heatwave conditions ease across UP; mercury drops 11°C in 5 days
stories.summary: Weather took a dramatic turn in Lucknow on Thursday night, with strong winds blowing at speeds of up to 60 kmph, followed by heavy rain. The intense storm led to power outages in several areas, while tin roofs and temporary structures were blown away. After 9 pm, electricity was disrupted in many localities including Alambagh, Krishnanagar, Mohanlalganj, Khadra, BKT and Faizullaganj. Areas such as Hazratganj, Balu Adda, Park Road and Gautam Palli were also affected by power cuts. The electricity department temporarily suspended supply in Mal, Rahimabad, Kakori, Gopra Mau, Rehman Khera and Nadarganj, before restoring it after around 20 minutes. Breakdowns were also reported on Baba Ka Purwa, Ahibaran Pur and Nishatganj New Hyderabad feeders, affecting nearly one lakh residents. Strong winds snapped tree branches across the city. The sudden weather change caused trouble for commuters heading home and pedestrians caught outdoors. In Sarojininagar, motorists were seen taking shelter under flyovers to escape the rain. The Meteorological Department had already issued an orange alert for rain and thunderstorms. On 26 April, the city had recorded a maximum temperature of 43°C. By 5 pm on Thursday, it had dropped to 31.7°C — a sharp fall of around 11.3°C in the last five days. See 5 pictures- Maximum temperature remained 31.7 degrees By 5 pm, the maximum temperature in Lucknow stood at 31.7°C, which was 7.8°C below normal. The minimum temperature was recorded at 23°C, 0.1°C below normal. Maximum humidity reached 75%, while minimum humidity stood at 46%. On Wednesday, the maximum temperature was 39.3°C, while the minimum was 27.3°C. Maximum humidity was 72%, with minimum humidity at 23%. Heat wave ends in Lucknow and the state The Meteorological Department reported that the weather mood has changed in Uttar Pradesh including Lucknow. With a sharp drop in temperature, the state has got relief from severe heat and hot winds. Currently, the hot wind situation in the state has almost ended. Gusty winds at speeds of 50 to 60 km per hour were recorded in Lucknow and many other parts of the state. Meteorological scientist Atul Kumar Singh said that this spell of unseasonal rain may continue till Friday. Due to this, the temperature in central and eastern Uttar Pradesh areas may drop by 2 to 4 degrees in the next 24 hours. See 2 morning pictures... Heatwave ends across Uttar Pradesh The Meteorological Department said weather conditions have changed across Uttar Pradesh, including Lucknow. A sharp fall in temperatures has brought relief from severe heat and heatwave conditions, which have now almost ended across the state. Gusty winds of 50–60 kmph were recorded in several parts of the state. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said this spell of unseasonal rain may continue till Friday. As a result, temperatures in central and eastern parts of Uttar Pradesh could drop by another 2 to 4 degrees over the next 24 hours. Another dip likely after 2–3 days Rain activity is expected to reduce during the first two to three days of May. After that, a fresh western disturbance is likely to become active on 4–5 May, which may bring another spell of rain across Lucknow and other parts of the state, leading to a further drop in temperatures.

Demikhov's work laid crucial groundwork for modern transplant medicine, influencing pioneers like Christiaan Barnard.

stories.title: From school to PG, girls now outnumber boys
stories.summary: India witnesses a significant shift as girls now lead in education, outperforming boys in school enrolment and higher education pass-outs. Researchers believe they could revolutionize dairy farming, even for urban households.

stories.title: Millions of graphene toothbrushes sold worldwide: Scientists reveal why people are buying them
stories.summary: New research from KAIST has clarified how graphene oxide's antibacterial properties work, revealing it selectively attacks harmful bacteria by targeting a specific lipid found in their membranes. This mechanism explains the success of graphene-based hygiene products and offers a novel approach to combating antibiotic resistance by physically disrupting bacterial structures.

stories.title: IShowSpeed plans space livestream after completing world tour goal
stories.summary: Popular streamer IShowSpeed revealed his ambitious plan to stream live from space after completing his goal of visiting all the world's countries. Having already traveled to 96 nations, he aims to finish his global tour in the next two to three years. Following this, he intends to embark on an unprecedented journey to space, potentially seeking assistance from Elon Musk.

stories.title: 'Time to say goodbye' :Jeffrey Epstein's suicide note revealed via former cellmate account, remains sealed by court
stories.summary: A recently surfaced report reveals Jeffrey Epstein penned a note before his 2019 death in a New York federal jail. Discovered by his cellmate, Nicholas Tartaglione, the handwritten message, now sealed by a judge, reportedly asserted Epstein's innocence and included the poignant phrase, "Time to say goodbye.

stories.title: Trump aide Josh Gruenbaum dropped from Ukraine, Iran roles: Here's why he was sidelined
stories.summary: Josh Gruenbaum, formerly an adviser to Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Russia-Ukraine and Iran policy, will now exclusively focus on Gaza Strip issues through the independent Board of Peace. This shift follows internal concerns about his working style, reducing his responsibilities from key foreign policy matters.

stories.title: Top 10 countries with the most skyscrapers in the world 2026: China, US, UAE and other leading nations
'Make Pluto a planet again': Nasa Administrator Jared Isaacman calls for status restoration at US Senate hearing
stories.summary: Nasa Administrator Jared Isaacman wants Pluto to be a planet again. He voiced this support in a Senate hearing. Nasa researchers are studying Pluto's status. Pluto was a planet until 2006. The International Astronomical Union reclassified it as a dwarf planet. This decision is still debated by scientists and the public. Isaacman believes Pluto should be a planet.

stories.title: Election Commission introduces QR code entry system for counting halls to ensure secure, tamper-free access
Kozhikode South
'Just spreading rumours': BJP dismisses TMC's ballot box 'tampering' charges amid ongoing protests
Mother convicted of baby’s murder after blaming another child
stories.summary: A Glasgow judge found Nicole Blain guilty of killing her infant daughter, Thea June Wilson, in Greenock. Evidence presented at trial showed the child suffered severe head injuries, including three skull fractures, consistent with forceful shaking and collision. Blain attempted to blame another child but her defense was contradicted by medical records and witness testimony.

stories.title: 'Alarming!' TMC posts video of 'gross electoral fraud', calls EC 'puppet'
stories.summary: The Trinamool Congress has accused the BJP and the Election Commission of "gross electoral fraud" and "murder of democracy" following alleged ballot box tampering. The party shared CCTV footage, claiming it shows unauthorized opening of ballot boxes ahead of the May 4th counting. TMC leaders have begun a sit-in protest, with Mamata Banerjee expected to visit the site.

stories.title: Quote of the day by German philosopher Immanuel Kant: “One who makes himself a worm cannot complain afterwards if people step on him.”
Britain extracted 25 million years of life and labour through slavery in Barbados: Report
stories.summary: British colonial practices in Barbados resulted in the loss of nearly 25 million years of life and forced labor from enslaved Africans, with estimated economic losses reaching £1.6 trillion. Researchers used economic modeling and historical data to quantify this exploitation, aiming to foster understanding and reconciliation rather than demanding payment.

stories.title: Consistency and strength highlight 30–39 age group 10k women’s category
Experience meets performance in 30–39 age group 10k men’s category
Move over TACO, NACHO takes over: Trump earns new nickname amid oil disruption from Strait of Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Market analysts have shifted from the 'TACO' nickname for President Trump to 'NACHO' amid escalating tensions over the Strait of Hormuz. This new label reflects growing skepticism that the crucial global energy route will reopen soon, despite ongoing diplomatic efforts and trade disputes.

stories.title: Nilambur
'Murder of democracy': TMC alleges EVM tampering in Kolkata strongroom; EC responds
As Trump nukes science, is India's brain drain ready for 'brain regain'?
stories.summary: The US President's dismissal of the National Science Board and other scientific bodies has sparked concerns about the erosion of scientific norms. This move, alongside funding cuts and grant cancellations, is prompting foreign-origin scientists to consider leaving the US, with India actively recruiting talent.

stories.title: Why Japan is recruiting bodybuilders and MMA fighters for elderly care
stories.summary: Japan's aging population is leading care providers to recruit physically strong individuals, including bodybuilders and athletes, to assist with demanding tasks like lifting and mobility support. This innovative approach aims to address labor shortages in the care sector and make the profession more appealing to younger workers by highlighting its active nature.

stories.title: Donald Trump to get Nobel Peace Prize in 2026? Committee says 287 candidates shortlisted
stories.summary: Over 287 candidates, including Donald Trump, are vying for the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. The Norwegian Nobel Committee Secretary noted significant renewal among nominees, emphasizing the prize's enduring relevance amidst global conflicts. While nominations are confidential, leaders from Cambodia, Israel, and Pakistan have reportedly put Trump forward, though this doesn't guarantee an endorsement.

stories.title: US tightens visa rules, requires applicants to declare no persecution concerns in home country
stories.summary: US embassies now require nonimmigrant visa applicants to declare they don't fear persecution back home. This new rule, aimed at preventing asylum claims upon arrival, asks applicants if they've faced harm or fear it upon return. Experts warn this could force individuals into dangerous migration routes, jeopardizing their safety and families.

stories.title: Forget Ronaldo: João Cancelo set for historic record no player has ever achieved if Barca win La Liga
stories.summary: João Cancelo is on the brink of a unique European football milestone, with a potential La Liga title at Barcelona set to make him the first player to win four of Europe’s “Big Five” leagues. Having already lifted trophies in Italy, England and Germany, the achievement would surpass Cristiano Ronaldo’s cross-league record and underline Cancelo’s unusual, globe-spanning career path.

stories.title: Machines take charge: China to deploy 8,500 robots in $1B push to automate its power grid
stories.summary: China is investing $1 billion in approximately 8,500 robots for its national power grid. These machines, including robot dogs and those with robotic arms, will enhance inspection and maintenance in challenging environments. This move aims to boost efficiency, safety, and reliability in electricity delivery, while also advancing China's AI and robotics ambitions.

stories.title: MP boat mishap: cruise capsizes in Jabalpur, 4 killed, rescue ops on
stories.summary: Tragedy struck in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, as a cruise boat capsized in Bargi Dam, resulting in four fatalities. Officials confirmed that while 15 individuals have been rescued, search operations continue for 12 still missing. Rescue teams are actively working to locate all passengers following the devastating incident.

stories.title: 'They call Trump Nazi, Hitler & still attend': Erika Kirk hits out at journalists for 'ultimate hypocrisy' at White House dinner
stories.summary: Erika Kirk, CEO of Turning Point USA, criticized journalists for labeling President Trump with extreme terms while attending the White House Correspondents' Dinner. She attended to confront media over coverage of her and her late husband, Charlie Kirk, who was murdered in 2025. Kirk linked the attempted White House shooting to a climate of dehumanization fueled by media narratives.

stories.title: ‘No place in Gulf, except at bottom of its waters’: Iran’s Khamenei slams ‘Great Satan’ US, rejects nuclear curbs
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei declared Iran's nuclear and missile capabilities non-negotiable, calling the US the "Great Satan" and asserting that foreigners have no place in the Persian Gulf. He emphasized that Iran's technological and military assets are national treasures to be protected by its population.

stories.title: Today's Chanakya exit poll: Mamata set to lose Bengal, status quo in Assam and Tamil Nadu; tight UDF–LDF race in Kerala
stories.summary: Today's Chanakya exit polls predict a landslide victory for the BJP in Assam, indicating a second term for Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma. In Kerala, the projections show a close contest between the incumbent LDF and the UDF, with the BJP expected to secure a few seats. Projections for West Bengal and Tamil Nadu are still awaited.

stories.title: ‘Iron Man’ Rodtang suffers rare second KO loss in retirement clash with fighter he previously beat in 80 secs
stories.summary: Takeru Segawa ended his career with a fifth-round stoppage of Rodtang “Iron Man” Jitmuangnon at ONE Samurai 1, claiming the interim flyweight kickboxing world title. The win avenged his 80-second knockout loss a year earlier, capping a 46–5 career. The bout saw Takeru overcome early pressure before dropping and finishing Rodtang in a dramatic reversal.

stories.title: Reform UK’s Zia Yusuf threatens to ban NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani from UK over kohinoor return call
Most decorated woman athlete with seven Olympic golds planning stunning LA28 comeback at 42
stories.summary: Allyson Felix is targeting a remarkable Olympic return at Los Angeles 2028, driven by the pull of competing at home rather than expectations of success. The most decorated woman in track and field history is balancing family life with a measured comeback attempt, aiming to test her limits once more, even as she openly acknowledges the challenges of returning at 42.

stories.title: Pingla assembly election results 2026
'We are forming govt of Maa, Mati, Manush': Bengal CM Mamata rejects exit polls giving BJP edge
stories.summary: West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee dismissed exit poll predictions, asserting the Trinamool Congress will secure a decisive victory. While most surveys indicated a close contest with a slight edge for the BJP, one poll projected a strong win for the TMC. Both parties expressed confidence in their respective wins.

stories.title: F1 to return in 2027 to country absent from calendar since 2021 under new multi-year agreement
stories.summary: The Turkish Grand Prix will return to the Formula 1 calendar in 2027 under a multi-year agreement confirmed on April 24, keeping Istanbul Park on the schedule through 2031. The move restores a circuit last used in 2021, known for its demanding layout and iconic Turn 8, as F1 continues reshaping its calendar with global expansion and venue changes.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Marie Curie: "There are sadistic scientists who hurry to hunt down error instead of establishing the truth."
Evening news wrap: SC asks Centre to consider abortion beyond 20 weeks for rape survivors; & more
'Words not enough': Netanyahu targets PM Starmer after UK stabbing incident
Emerging women athletes: Under-29 10K category reflects talent and ambition
Young talent shines: Under-29 10K (Male) category delivers strong performances at Times Internet Half Marathon
Mount St. Helens eruption: How Gophers transformed a barren land in 43 years
‘Not necessary to humiliate me with arrest’: Pawan Khera in SC amid passport row case
Nine arrested in UK raids on Ahmadi group in Crewe over ‘modern slavery’ and rape allegations
'Sonia Gandhi takes our decisions': Kharge on speculations over change of CM in Karnataka
stories.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge downplayed the Karnataka chief ministerial tussle between Siddaramaiah and DK Shivakumar, stating the party will resolve the "confusion soon." This comes amid speculation fueled by a reported power-sharing agreement and a statement from Home Minister G Parameshwara suggesting Kharge could be a suitable CM.

stories.title: London stabbing declared ‘terrorist incident’; UK announces £25m security boost for Jewish community
Saudi Arabia executes Iraqi nationals convicted in northern border drug smuggling case
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has executed several Iraqi nationals. They were convicted of attempting to smuggle narcotics into the kingdom. The executions followed a thorough legal process. Saudi authorities are intensifying their crackdown on drug trafficking. This campaign targets organized criminal networks. The kingdom vows to impose strict punishments against smugglers.

stories.title: UAE announces petrol, diesel prices for May 2026 as fuel rates jump by up to 10% across Emirates
stories.summary: UAE motorists will face higher fuel costs in May 2026 as petrol prices see another significant increase. This marks the third consecutive monthly hike, driven by global oil market instability and geopolitical tensions. The latest revisions mean higher expenses for daily commutes and businesses reliant on transportation.

stories.title: Iran at UN accuses US of nuclear double standards, misuse of NPT platform
stories.summary: Iran's UN mission accused the US of misrepresenting its nuclear program at a review conference, deflecting from Washington's own violations. Tehran insists its enriched uranium is IAEA-supervised, with no diversion. Meanwhile, Iran's envoy warned that regional stability hinges on ending aggression and respecting its sovereignty, urging the UN Security Council to intervene amidst escalating tensions.

stories.title: India among worst-hit as hepatitis deaths stay high despite global gains: WHO report
stories.summary: India faces a significant hepatitis burden, contributing to a high number of global deaths. Despite progress in reducing infections, the world is off track to meet 2030 elimination targets due to gaps in vaccination, screening, and treatment access. Viral hepatitis remains a major public health threat.

stories.title: NMC nod to cardiology diploma after 20-year wait; 1,700 doctors’ degrees recognised
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has recognized the Post Graduate Diploma in Clinical Cardiology (PGDCC), validating degrees for 1,700 doctors trained between 2006-2013. This move by IGNOU, now redesignated as Clinical Cardio Physician (Non-Invasive), aims to address the critical shortage of cardiology specialists in underserved regions and bridge the urban-rural healthcare gap.

stories.title: 'Strait of Trump': US President shares new map naming Hormuz after himself
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump shared a modified map renaming the Strait of Hormuz as the "Strait of Trump," following claims that a naval blockade against Iran could last for months. This development occurs as Iran rejects US claims about economic damage and criticizes the blockade strategy, with its parliament speaker calling the advice "junk."

stories.title: 'Imagine the pain, humiliation': Supreme Court urges Centre to allow abortion beyond 20 weeks for rape survivors
stories.summary: The Supreme Court urged the Centre to consider amending laws to allow rape survivors to terminate pregnancies beyond 20 weeks, emphasizing no time limit in such cases. The bench highlighted the lifelong trauma for a child survivor and the need for the decision to rest with the survivor and her parents, with AIIMS offering counsel.

stories.title: I-PAC co-founder and director Vinesh Chandela gets bail in money laundering case
stories.summary: I-PAC director Vinesh Chandela has been granted bail by a Delhi court in a money laundering case. The Enforcement Directorate did not oppose his release, citing his cooperation with the investigation. Chandela was arrested earlier this month as part of a probe into financial dealings linked to the firm and an alleged coal scam.

stories.title: 'We didn't fall for nuclear bluff': Rajnath Singh slams Pakistan, explains why Op Sindoor was halted
stories.summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh stated India voluntarily halted Operation Sindoor on its own terms, asserting readiness for a prolonged conflict with Pakistan, which he labeled the "epicentre of International Terrorism." He emphasised India's "zero tolerance" for terrorism and its sponsors, highlighting the nation's robust military capabilities and resolve against nuclear threats.

stories.title: IShowSpeed health status: Social media icon collapsed on livestream after 12 hours of intense streaming on Caribbean tour
stories.summary: Popular YouTuber and livestreamer IShowSpeed scared fans after he appeared to pass out during a live stream in St. Maarten. The incident happened during his ongoing Caribbean tour, where he has been streaming from multiple countries. A short video clip quickly went viral on social media, showing the 21-year-old looking extremely tired before collapsing while people nearby rushed to help him.

stories.title: 'Fellow MLAs will remain outside': Punjab CM to meet President Murmu over seven AAP RS MPs joining BJP
stories.summary: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann will meet President Murmu on May 5 to "safeguard the mandate of the people" following the defection of seven AAP Rajya Sabha MPs to the BJP. Mann, accompanied by party MLAs, will press for the "recall" of the MPs, though legal provisions for such a recall are absent.

stories.title: Exit poll results 2026 for West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Assam, Kerala, Puducherry: Explained in 5 charts
stories.summary: Exit polls suggest a mixed verdict across states as West Bengal anticipates a hung assembly, potentially ending Mamata Banerjee's tenure. Tamil Nadu might see actor Vijay's TVK emerge as a significant force, challenging the established duopoly. Assam favors a BJP hat-trick, while Kerala's Left government faces a potential defeat. Puducherry's NDA is expected to retain power.

SC: Can't take away right to speedy trial due to gravity of case
Matter of religion is a matter of conscience, not for debate: SC
India needs to look at its national interests with regard to the Gulf of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran and the US remain locked in a standoff, with Iran effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz and the US imposing a naval blockade. Both actions disrupt global commons, while escalating rhetoric and social media influence commodity prices worldwide. India, heavily reliant on regional energy flows, faces significant economic fallout from this 'dual blockade'.

stories.title: NMC nod to cardiology diploma after years of wait
7 buried alive in Bengaluru hospital wall collapse
Sacred Piprahwa relics of Buddha reach Ladakh as Leh marks Buddha Purnima
"Make your life miserable": Candace Owens hits back at Donald Trump over “vile” remark during livestream
stories.summary: Candace Owens addressed criticism from Donald Trump during a livestream after he called her “vile” in a Truth Social post. Responding with sarcasm, she questioned the motive behind his remarks and suggested political pressure may be involved. Owens framed the attack as part of an ongoing pattern, hinting at deeper dynamics while avoiding a detailed rebuttal of the claims.

stories.title: Exit polls differ on West Bengal, Tamil Nadu; give Assam to BJP, Kerala to Cong
stories.summary: Exit polls suggest a BJP-led alliance victory in Assam and a UDF win in Kerala, potentially leaving the Left out of power in any state. Puducherry is expected to see the AINRC-BJP combine retain power. Tamil Nadu and West Bengal present a mixed picture, with some polls indicating a tight race in Tamil Nadu and differing predictions for West Bengal.

stories.title: India, UAE in talks for stopover by Modi next month
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi may make a brief stopover in the UAE next month during his European tour. Discussions are ongoing for this potential visit, which would underscore India's strong strategic partnership with the Gulf nation. This stopover would allow India to express solidarity following Iran's strikes on GCC countries.

stories.title: Araghchi dials Jaishankar to discuss West Asia situation

Flights resume at Jodhpur runway as IAF’s Dornier lands after runway upgrade

PM inaugurates Ganga Expressway, says it will be linked to Haridwar
Vote-shy Kolkata catches up with Bengal, well, almost
Candace Owens breaks silence after Andrew Kolvet chat leak as Charlie Kirk show clip leaves viewers uneasy
stories.summary: Candace Owens faced fresh online backlash after a strange Charlie Kirk show clip and a leaked chat screenshot went viral. A controversial line from the chat sparked strong reactions, but Owens said it was taken out of context and meant as a joke. The debate now centers on authenticity, editing, and whether the full story is being shown.

stories.title: Paths of 'Singham' & 'Pushpa' don't cross, Falta focuses on taped EVM
stories.summary: Falta constituency witnessed a high-stakes election day with IPS Ajay Pal Sharma, dubbed 'Singham', patrolling while TMC candidate Jahangir Khan, 'Pushpa', monitored from his control room. Despite charged rhetoric, the anticipated confrontation didn't materialize, overshadowed by EVM complaints, leading to a repoll in Falta.

stories.title: This nanogenerator turns seawater evaporation into electricity-and it never stops
DRDO, Navy conduct maiden salvo launch of 2 anti-ship missiles from chopper off Odisha coast
Bhowanipore votes, Didi breaks poll-day routine & Suvendu says, 'I like this fear'
stories.summary: A tense election day in Bhowanipore saw Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and rival Suvendu Adhikari narrowly miss each other, highlighting a bitter personal contest. Both leaders traded accusations of intimidation and rigging amidst high voter turnout. Incidents of clashes and alleged assaults by central forces were reported, escalating the political heat.

stories.title: Was Jeffrey Epstein building a 'mosque' on his private island? Records show rare Islamic artefacts brought from Middle East
stories.summary: Disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein cultivated Middle Eastern connections and acquired rare Islamic artifacts, including pieces from the Kaaba, for a building on his private island he called a 'mosque.' Documents reveal his interest in Islamic architecture and his pursuit of Saudi Arabian business opportunities before his arrest and death.

stories.title: Army set to hold first-ever multilateral military drill involving 11 countries from May 18 to 31
Sacred relics of Buddha from National Museum reach Ladakh as Leh marks Buddha Purnima
Record turnout over two phases harbinger of change in Bengal: Modi
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that Bengal's record voter turnout signals a change, expressing confidence in the BJP's victory. He also predicted NDA's retention of Assam and Puducherry, with potential surprises in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Modi highlighted the high turnout as a reflection of fear-free elections and voters' awareness of their democratic rights.

stories.title: 2028 Chandrayaan-5 launch site preparation begins: ISRO team visits Japan for assessment
92.6% turnout in Phase 2 takes Bengal total to record 92.9%
stories.summary: West Bengal witnessed an unprecedented voter turnout of 92.9% across two phases, surpassing previous records and nearing India's highest. This surge, particularly in Kolkata, is attributed to voter roll corrections and enhanced security. Despite a reduced electorate, more votes were cast, with women outvoting men. Officials are investigating complaints of vote tampering.

stories.title: D4vd makes unusual request ahead of hearing, judge responds with a twist
stories.summary: D4vd faces a crucial court hearing for serious charges including murder. His request to wear formal clothes instead of jail attire was denied by the judge. However, the court did approve a haircut for him before the May 1 hearing. This unusual pre-hearing scenario adds a peculiar twist to the ongoing legal proceedings.

stories.title: 12 labourers killed, 20 injured as van overturns, crashes into SUV in Madhya Pradesh's Dhar
'Is a President allowed to go on a space mission?': Trump jokes as Artemis II astronauts visit White House
stories.summary: President Trump expressed confidence in NASA's ability to land astronauts on the Moon before his potential second term ends in 2029. He met with the Artemis II crew at the White House, celebrating their recent deep-space mission. This comes as NASA targets a crewed lunar landing in 2028, though development timelines for landers remain a concern.

stories.title: Controversial streamer Clavicular accused of abuse and fraud in explosive lawsuit by influencer
stories.summary: Influencer Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza has filed a lawsuit against streamer Clavicular, real name Braden Peters, alleging abuse, fraud, and emotional harm. Mendoza claims Peters exploited her trust, promising career advancement but instead causing significant distress and damage. The suit details accusations of non-consensual sexual encounters and an unauthorized facial injection. Peters' lawyer denies all claims.

stories.title: London Marathon winner’s massive payday revealed as he names first purchase after historic run
stories.summary: Sebastian Sawe’s record-breaking London Marathon run has delivered a life-changing payday, with prize money and bonuses pushing his earnings toward seven figures. The Kenyan star has already outlined how he plans to use it, focusing on building a home, buying a car for his family and supporting his local community, turning sporting success into lasting impact beyond the race.

stories.title: 'Return Koh-i-Noor diamond': Zohran Mamdani quips on crown jewel handover during King Charles' New York visit
stories.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani indicated he would urge King Charles III to return the Koh-i-Noor diamond during the monarch's visit to the city. The suggestion came as the King and Queen Camilla attended engagements, including a visit to the National 9/11 Memorial & Museum. The Koh-i-Noor, a disputed colonial-era artifact, has been a point of contention for centuries.

stories.title: Urine drug tests on drivers conducted as part of ‘Nasha-Mukt’ J&K drive
4,300-year-old gold-covered mummy found sealed in deep Egyptian shaft, shocks archaeologists
Ex-FBI chief James Comey surrenders in 'threat' case against Donald Trump; what was '86 47' post?
stories.summary: Former FBI Director James Comey surrendered to US authorities after being charged with threatening President Donald Trump via a social media post. Prosecutors allege his Instagram message, featuring seashells and numbers, conveyed a threat. Comey maintains his innocence, calling the charges vindictive, and plans to fight them in court.

stories.title: Putin, Trump hold 90-minute call on Iran, Ukraine war: Russia proposes Kyiv ceasefire for Victory Day
stories.summary: Presidents Putin and Trump held a 1.5-hour call discussing the Middle East war and Ukraine. Putin backed Trump's Iran ceasefire extension, viewing it as a stabilizing move. He also proposed a temporary ceasefire in Ukraine for Victory Day, aiming to advance peace negotiations.

stories.title: Iran ‘choking like a stuffed pig’: Trump digs in on Hormuz blockade; Tehran warns ‘unprecedented action’
stories.summary: United States President Donald Trump states the naval blockade on Iran will continue until Tehran agrees to a nuclear deal. Military strikes are also being planned. Iran warns of unprecedented action if pressure persists. The situation is volatile, with potential for negotiation or confrontation.

stories.title: Poll of exit polls 2026: Bengal cliffhanger, Congress in Kerala; status quo in Tamil Nadu, Assam, Puducherry - predictions decoded
stories.summary: Exit polls released on Wednesday after the conclusion of voting across four states and one Union Territory (UT) offered an indecisive picture, where entrenched incumbencies, rising challengers and new entrants are simultaneously may shape electoral outcomes if the exit polls numbers hold. With results scheduled for May 4, the projections reflect both continuity and churn across regions, underscoring how state-specific dynamics continue to define voter behaviour.

stories.title: Trump halts speech in awkward moment to praise Rory McIlroy’s Masters win at White House dinner
stories.summary: At a White House state dinner, Donald Trump broke from his prepared speech to publicly praise Rory McIlroy’s Masters triumph, creating an unscripted moment that briefly disrupted the evening’s formal tone. Yet despite Trump’s enthusiasm, McIlroy will skip the upcoming Cadillac Championship at Trump National Doral, opting instead for rest before returning ahead of the PGA Championship.

stories.title: 4 am fury, 24/7 gridlock: Trump takes world into long, hot Hormuz summer
stories.summary: President Trump has directed aides to prepare for a prolonged naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, aiming to choke Iran's oil exports and force concessions without triggering wider conflict. This strategy is causing global energy disruptions, with rising gasoline prices impacting American consumers and forcing other nations to scramble for alternative supplies.

stories.title: 'I really didn't know what was going on': JD Vance recalls White House dinner security breach
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance described the chaotic scene at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner after a suspected armed man allegedly attempted to breach security and target President Trump. Vance recounted hearing unclear noises and seeing people ducking under tables before a security agent instructed him to leave.

stories.title: Who is Amy Beck? Noah Beck’s mother suspended after TikTok video resurfaces amid Haley Beck controversy
stories.summary: Amy Beck, mother of Noah Beck, was placed on leave from her Arizona teaching job after an old TikTok video resurfaced online. The clip sparked strong reactions from parents and led to a school investigation. The case has gained more attention due to ongoing issues involving her daughter Haley Beck, with no final decision yet announced.

stories.title: West Bengal logs record 91.66% turnout in phase 2, sporadic violence reported across districts
stories.summary: West Bengal witnessed a record voter turnout exceeding 91% in the second phase of assembly elections, contributing to an overall 92.47% across two phases, the highest since Independence. Despite high participation, sporadic incidents of violence and vandalism were reported from various locations, prompting the Election Commission to seek reports and ensure fair polling.

stories.title: The King of Comedy: How Charles III used humour to reprimand Donald Trump in the US Congress
stories.summary: There is, rather conveniently, an actual novel called The Two Georges which imagines a world in which George Washington and King George III settle their differences and the American Revolution never happens. In that version of history, America remains within the British system, the empire adapts, and everyone carries on with a slightly different flag and a great deal more politeness. Charles’s joke worked because it gestured at that absurd possibility, only to return the room to reality. The revolution did happen. The king did lose. The republic did win. The story was settled.

stories.title: White House dinner attack: Man charged in Trump assassination bid took photo with knife before assault
stories.summary: A California man, Cole Allen, is accused of attempting to assassinate President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner. Prosecutors revealed he photographed himself armed before the attack, which involved firing a shotgun at security. Allen, who had planned his actions, faces multiple charges.

stories.title: After giving away $26 billion in philanthropy, MacKenzie Scott’s wealth remains largely unchanged — here's why
stories.summary: MacKenzie Scott has donated over $26 billion since 2019, yet remains extremely wealthy because her fortune is tied to Amazon stock. As share values rise, her wealth continues to grow, allowing her to give at an unprecedented scale without a proportional decline in net worth.

stories.title: ‘Judicial restraint needed’: VHP hits out at Allahabad HC remarks in madrasa case
Tamil Nadu exit polls 2026: Kejriwal breakthrough or Prashant Kishor's 'farsh' moment — what will it be for Vijay?
stories.summary: Exit polls present a stark contrast for Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam in the 2026 Tamil Nadu elections. While most predict a spoiler role with 10-24 seats, one outlier suggests a Kejriwal-like breakthrough of 98-120 seats. The outcome hinges on converting star power into grassroots strength, unlike Prashant Kishor's Bihar debut.

stories.title: Donald Trump's approval rating falls amid Iran war, surge in fuel prices and rising cost-of-living
stories.summary: President Trump's approval rating has dropped to 34%, its lowest point, amid growing public dissatisfaction over the rising cost of living and the ongoing conflict with Iran. Economic concerns, particularly a 40% surge in gasoline prices following military action against Iran, are driving this discontent, impacting households and the Republican Party ahead of midterm elections.

stories.title: Treasure alert: 63 Anglo-Saxon coins uncovered in Worcestershire linked to the Viking age
Puducherry exit polls 2026: NDA likely to retain power; Congress, TVK lag in fragmented fight
stories.summary: Puducherry's 2026 elections saw a massive 89.83% voter turnout, with exit polls suggesting a tight race. The ruling NDA, led by AINRC-BJP, appears to have a slight edge over the Congress-DMK alliance. A new force, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, has also made its presence felt in several key constituencies, potentially fragmenting the results.

stories.title: Bengal exit polls 2026: Combined projections point to neck-and-neck TMC-BJP race; hung house likely
Kerala exit polls 2026: UDF predicted to win coastal state in neck-and-neck contest with LDF

stories.title: Meet Dattatreya Ramchandra Kaprekar: The Indian mathematician who discovered a ‘ghost number’ that always returns to itself
stories.summary: A humble schoolteacher, Dattatreya Ramchandra Kaprekar, discovered the remarkable 6174 constant through simple number experimentation. This number, reached by a specific digit rearrangement process, became a 'ghost number' due to its fixed-point behavior. Initially overlooked, Kaprekar's work gained international acclaim, influencing math education and computer science with its elegant demonstration of iterative computation.

stories.title: Why a gunman at the White House Correspondents' Dinner epitomises American idiosyncracy
stories.summary: Jean Paul-Sartre once said: Freedom is what you do with what’s been done to you, and America – with its freedom from Britain and other colonial powers – develop its own peculiarities, one of which is the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, a night where the press and the White House ostensibly bury their differences over a few shots. Normally those shots are jokes like Obama’s anger translator or Reagan dialling in after an assassination attempt, but this year they came from the barrel of a deranged gunman who had managed to waltz past security.

The court emphasized that convictions require proof, not mere suspicion.

Warmer weather is expected midweek, with a shift to milder air by Thursday, potentially peaking at 24°C by Friday.

He was later taken to Naya Nagar Police Station, where a case was registered against him under charges including attempted murder and promoting enmity between communities.

stories.title: 'Politics has its place': Akhilesh Yadav visits BJP MLA who was injured while burning his effigy

Party workers raised slogans, burned his effigy, and held placards expressing anger over his switch. This follows similar demonstrations in Ludhiana against MP Rajinder Gupta.

stories.title: Indian-origin Trump aide slammed for her outfit joke after White House shooting: 'I lost some professional respect for you'
Kash Patel seen ‘scrolling his phone’ as agents rush guests from DC shooting scare
'Dil' of India turns choking lungs: Can Delhi fix its pollution crisis?
stories.summary: The air quality crisis in Delhi is an ongoing battle, often leading to emergency protocols like the GRAP being activated as pollution levels soar. While these short-term fixes bring momentary relief, they overlook the fundamental problems. To forge a path toward long-lasting improvements, we must commit to a year-round strategy to curb emissions from vehicles, factories, and farming activities.

stories.title: Himanta wife passport row: Pawan Khera moves SC for anticipatory bail after setback from Guwahati HC
stories.summary: The Gauhati high court had on April 24 rejected Khera's plea for anticipatory bail in the case registered against him by the Crime Branch of Assam Police in Guwahati. The case against Khera was registered after he claimed at a press brief that ​​Assam CM's wife Riniki Bhuyan "holds multiple foreign passports and undisclosed assets abroad".

stories.title: 'Bizarre': Former student of White House shooting suspect says Cole Allen seemed like a completely average guy
'UCC rollout, triple talaq ban, end to polygamy': Amit Shah rolls out BJP's key promises at Bengal rally
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled major BJP promises for West Bengal, including implementing Uniform Civil Code, banning triple talaq, and ending polygamy. He also pledged financial aid for women and unemployed youth, and a crackdown on cattle smuggling. Shah highlighted national security achievements and vowed to expel illegal infiltrators if the BJP wins.

stories.title: Where are Kaddu and Dholu? Delhi Airport faces heat over missing dogs
stories.summary: A Delhi court has also intervened, asking local police to explain why no FIR has been registered so far. The next hearing is scheduled for April 29. Activists warn that any confirmed acts of cruelty could invite strict penalties under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act and the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita.

stories.title: 'Trump and admin officials': Acting AG reveals who was gunman's target at WH shooting
stories.summary: A lone gunman, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, disrupted the White House Correspondents' Association dinner, exchanging fire with law enforcement. Investigators suspect he may have targeted Trump administration members. Allen traveled from California and was found with multiple weapons. President Trump was safely evacuated during the incident.

stories.title: Mali violence escalates: Defence minister Sadio Camara killed in 'terrorist attack'
stories.summary: Mali's security crisis deepened with the killing of Defence Minister Sadio Camara in an attack on his residence. Coordinated strikes by separatist fighters and Al-Qaeda-linked militants targeted Bamako and other cities, marking a significant escalation. The separatists confirmed an alliance with JNIM, complicating counterinsurgency efforts.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Trump shooting scare at White House dinner; AAP seeks termination of 7 rebel MPs & more
stories.summary: Donald Trump was evacuated unharmed after gunfire at a White House dinner. The AAP is seeking the termination of seven rebel MPs. Rahul Gandhi condemned the killing of a Congress worker in West Bengal. Ishan Kishan shared a light-hearted moment with a young cricketer. Chernobyl has become a wildlife sanctuary 40 years after the nuclear accident.

stories.title: Indian man arrested in Texas after attacking woman and biting her child; student visa was revoked in 2025
Weak muscles, falling risk: AIIMS study finds gut link in elderly
stories.summary: Published in Geriatrics & Gerontology International, the study led by Sudeep Mathew George and Prasun Chatterjee examined 30 adults above the age of 60 and found that those with sarcopenia—a condition marked by gradual muscle loss—had significantly less diverse gut bacteria, a marker of poorer overall health. The findings support the emerging concept of a “gut–muscle axis,” where disruptions in gut microbes may affect muscle strength through immune, metabolic and nutritional pathways.

stories.title: World Malaria Day-- WHO clears first malaria drug for newborns, flags new tests as old ones fail
stories.summary: The WHO prequalification clears the way for countries and global agencies to procure the medicine for public health programmes, expanding access to a quality-assured treatment for one of the most vulnerable groups. While the immediate impact is expected in high-burden regions such as Africa, the approval also opens the door for countries like India to adopt the formulation through national programmes if needed.

stories.title: AIIMS likely to get interim head as search for new director to start
stories.summary: Names doing the rounds include senior faculty such as Dr Nikhil Tandon, professor and head of endocrinology, Dr Radhika Tandon, Chief, Professor of Ophthalmology and Prof Sandeep Chauhan head of cardiac anaesthesia department, though sources cautioned that no decision has been taken yet. “There are established conventions, but nothing is final yet. Typically, the senior-most person is asked to hold charge,” a senior doctor said.

stories.title: Lights, camera...gone? The slow fade of India's OG photostudios
stories.summary: Neighbourhood photo studios, once bustling hubs, are now struggling as digital cameras and smartphones have made photography an everyday habit. Photographers lament the loss of business, with many now relying on outdoor events and regional film projects to survive. This shift reflects a societal change in how memories are captured and consumed.

stories.title: Stayed at Hilton, no metal detectors: How suspect slipped past security, carried out shooting at WH Correspondents’ Dinner
stories.summary: An armed man breached security at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner, exchanging fire with law enforcement before being apprehended. Investigators believe gaps in outer security layers allowed the suspect, staying at the hotel, to approach the event. He was tackled by Secret Service agents near a checkpoint.

stories.title: West Bengal elections: PM Modi pledges citizenship for Matua Namasudras under CAA
stories.summary: PM Modi also offered prayers at Thakurbari, the main temple of the Matua Mahasangha at Thakurnagar in West Bengal's North 24 Parganas district before his poll rally in the area. His visit to the headquarters of the community, housing the shrines of the sect's founders Hari Chand and Guru Chand Thakur, is seen as an outreach to Matua voters who influence at least 34 assembly seats directly and another two dozen along the Bangladesh border.

stories.title: 'Data over dynasties': Grok picks Narendra Modi over Rahul Gandhi in hypothetical vote for PM
stories.summary: Grok, the AI chatbot, has sparked renewed debate by hypothetically stating it would vote for Prime Minister Narendra Modi if it were an Indian citizen. The chatbot cited economic growth, infrastructure, and digital transformation as reasons for its preference, contrasting this with Rahul Gandhi's focus on welfare critiques.

stories.title: 'Put it together, ran towards ballroom': Volunteer recalls WH gunman assembled 'long weapon' in 'makeshift room'
stories.summary: A White House Correspondents' Dinner volunteer reported the suspected gunman assembled a "long weapon" in an unsecured area near a terrace entrance before the attack. The suspect then moved toward the ballroom, firing shots and causing panic among guests and staff. The gunman, identified as Cole Allen, was arrested after allegedly entering the Washington Hilton hotel.

stories.title: Trump’s Golden Dome missile shield faces budget squeeze despite Pentagon push
stories.summary: President Trump's ambitious Golden Dome missile defense initiative faces significant hurdles. Doubts are mounting over funding, congressional backing, and technical feasibility, despite Pentagon assurances. The project's immense cost, potentially trillions, is a major concern for lawmakers, particularly Republicans wary of budget reconciliation tactics ahead of elections. Key components are slated for 2028.

stories.title: Mother and young child die in tragic water incident at west London park, police say no foul play suspected
AAP sends petition to Rajya Sabha Chair to terminate 7 MPs who moved to BJP
stories.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party has urged the Rajya Sabha Chairman to disqualify seven MPs who defected to the BJP, citing constitutional experts who believe they are liable for disqualification. This move follows the MPs' departure, sparking a legal and political dispute over anti-defection rules.

stories.title: Meet Emma Rodriguez: US Army pilot and wife of freshly drafted Dolphins linebacker Jacob Rodriguez
stories.summary: Jacob Rodriguez’s NFL Draft moment wasn’t just about football, as cameras caught him celebrating with his wife Emma, an active-duty US Army Black Hawk pilot. While he begins his career with the Miami Dolphins, their story stands out for a different reason—two demanding paths running side by side, shaped by distance, discipline, and shared ambition.

stories.title: Residents evacuated after car explosion outside Northern Ireland police station
'I've studied assassinations': Trump on why White House dinner shooting keeps happening to him
stories.summary: Following a shooting scare at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, President Trump stated he has studied assassinations and believes impactful leaders are often targeted. He linked the incident to his presidency's influence, suggesting those unhappy with changes are responsible. Trump also commented on the personal risks of political life and criticized the hotel's security.

stories.title: West Bengal Assembly elections: EC to hold key readiness review in Kolkata ahead of Phase 2 polling
stories.summary: Ahead of West Bengal's second phase of assembly elections on April 29, a high-level coordination meeting will be held in Kolkata to assess poll preparedness. Senior officials will discuss force deployment, vulnerability mapping, and readiness for smooth, free, and fair polling in key districts.

stories.title: Developer, CalTech pass out — White House dinner shooter Cole Thomas Allen a 'highly educated tutor'
'If you're not close enough, your photo is not good enough': Remembering Raghu Rai
stories.summary: Legendary photographer Raghu Rai, who shaped India's visual memory for over five decades, passed away on Sunday. His iconic images, from the Bhopal Gas tragedy to portraits of national figures, gave permanence to history. Rai believed visual history was more important than fine art, emphasizing closeness to truth in his immersive photographic practice.

stories.title: 'Our nuclear scientists made Bharat proud': Top quotes from PM Modi's 'Mann ki Baat' address
'Not democracy, but TMC's reign of thuggery': Rahul Gandhi over killing of Congress worker
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has strongly condemned the murder of Congress worker Debdeep Chatterjee in West Bengal, attributing the killing to "TMC thugs" following phase-1 polling. He accused the ruling party of replacing democracy with "thuggery" and demanded immediate arrests, harsh punishment, and compensation for the victim's family, vowing to uphold non-violence.

stories.title: Countries with the most millionaires in 2026: The US tops the global list, China and France follow
More than a dozen threats & assassination attempts — Timeline of attacks against Donald Trump
stories.summary: A shooting attempt at the White House Correspondents' Dinner led to the immediate evacuation of President Trump and other officials. This incident adds to a long list of threats and security scares faced by Trump, including armed intruders, assassination plots, and poison mail, making him a frequent target.

stories.title: Bomb attack kills 14, injures 38 in Colombia weeks before presidential election
stories.summary: A deadly highway bomb attack in Colombia's Cauca region has killed 14 and injured 38. The blast occurred as assailants blocked the road. Authorities blame FARC dissidents. This violence escalates security concerns just weeks before the presidential election. The attack follows a wave of incidents targeting public infrastructure across southwestern Colombia.

stories.title: 'Relieved to learn Trump, First Lady safe': PM Modi says violence has no place in democracy
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi expressed relief after a shooting incident at the White House Correspondents' Dinner. President Trump, the First Lady, and Vice President Vance were unharmed. The assailant, armed with a shotgun, was apprehended by the Secret Service after injuring an agent, who was protected by a vest. Panic ensued as guests sought cover.

stories.title: ‘I just want to go home’: Tearful Erika Kirk escorted out after White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting
stories.summary: Erika Kirk was seen being escorted from the White House Correspondents' Dinner in tears after gunfire caused panic and evacuation. The incident evoked sympathy due to her husband Charlie Kirk's death last year. The dinner was disrupted by a shooting near the security screening area, leading to a lockdown and the arrest of a suspect.

stories.title: Engine fire on SWISS Delhi-Zurich flight during take off roll; aircraft evacuated on runway
stories.summary: Six passengers were hospitalized after a SWISS flight from Delhi to Zurich was evacuated on the runway due to an engine fire during takeoff. The Airbus A330's engine number one failed at 104 knots, prompting the crew to abort the takeoff and evacuate all 232 passengers and crew using emergency slides.

stories.title: Trump evacuated from media dinner after gunshots; supporters say another assassination attempt
stories.summary: Shots rang out near the White House Correspondents' Association dinner, prompting the hurried evacuation of President Trump and other dignitaries. The Secret Service apprehended one individual and is investigating the incident, which occurred shortly before Trump was to deliver his keynote speech.

stories.title: From Ronald Reagan to Donald Trump: How Washington Hilton hotel became scene of panic once again
stories.summary: Panic erupted at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Dinner when gunshots were reported, mirroring a similar incident involving President Reagan decades prior. Secret Service agents swiftly escorted President Trump to safety as attendees took cover. The shooter was apprehended, and Trump praised security efforts.

stories.title: US Prez & First Lady safe after shooting at White House: Trump holds press conference
Mexico: 2 dead US agents had no permission to raid drug lab
'Quite an evening': Trump wanted 'the show to go on' after shooting at White House Correspondents' Dinner
stories.summary: Shots were fired near the White House Correspondents' Dinner venue, prompting President Trump's temporary evacuation as a security precaution. The shooter was apprehended by law enforcement, who acted swiftly and bravely. Trump confirmed the incident and indicated plans to reschedule the event, emphasizing the safety of all attendees.

stories.title: Minority group condemns brutal murder of Nayan Sadhu in Bangladesh
‘Taken offsite’: Who was the shooter at Trump’s White House dinner? First image emerges
stories.summary: President Donald Trump was evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Dinner after shots were fired, with the suspect apprehended by the Secret Service. An individual reportedly attempted to enter with a gun but was stopped before reaching the ballroom. Trump praised law enforcement and urged the event to continue.

stories.title: Shooter fires 5 to 8 shots at White House dinner, Trump evacuated - what we know so far
stories.summary: A major security incident disrupted the White House Correspondents' Association dinner, forcing the evacuation of President Trump and other top officials. Witnesses reported hearing five to eight gunshots, and a shooter was confirmed by law enforcement, though details remain unclear. No injuries were immediately reported among the hundreds of guests.

A 30-year-old Californian man, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, was apprehended by the Secret Service after allegedly attempting to breach security with a firearm. An officer was reportedly shot but is expected to recover.

Power demand defies forecasts, officials say consumption likely to surge further
stories.summary: India's electricity demand hit a record 252 GW on April 24. Soaring temperatures across the nation drove this surge. Air conditioner usage increased significantly in homes and businesses. This peak demand surpassed previous records. The power ministry anticipates further increases as heatwaves continue. Officials expect demand to rise even higher in the coming days.

Naidu: Must unite to tackle structural gaps
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu advocated for women's reservation and growth-led welfare, emphasizing wealth generation through reforms and investment. He also suggested encouraging a higher birth rate to maintain India's demographic advantage, urging a collective approach to structural challenges.

20 years in making: LeBron and Bronny James create NBA playoff history with first father-son alley-oop
stories.summary: LeBron James and Bronny James made NBA playoff history with the league’s first father-son scoring connection, as LeBron set up an alley-oop finished by Bronny in Game 3 against the Houston Rockets. Beyond the highlight, the moment underscored LeBron’s unmatched longevity, allowing their careers to overlap in a meaningful, competitive playoff setting rather than a symbolic appearance.

No Iran-US peace talks 2.0! How Pakistan's bid to mediate a breakthrough fell short
stories.summary: Pakistan's efforts to mediate US-Iran talks faltered as Tehran refused direct engagement, conveying demands through Islamabad. US President Trump subsequently canceled his delegation's visit, citing a lack of meaningful progress. The diplomatic deadlock persists, with Iran shifting its focus to Oman and Russia.

stories.title: 'Too much time wasted': Trump scraps US envoys' visit to Pakistan, says Iran can 'call' for talks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump canceled a planned trip by his envoys to Pakistan to meet Iranian leaders, citing wasted travel time and confusion within Iran's leadership. He asserted the US holds the upper hand and urged Iran to initiate talks. This decision has diminished Pakistan's role in facilitating US-Iran discussions.

stories.title: 110,000 devotees flock to Kedarnath in 3 days; temple leaders hail seamless yatra arrangements by Uttarakhand govt
'See India as civilisation, not nation': Isha founder Sadhguru at IIT2026 meet in US
stories.summary: At the IIT2026 Global Conference, Sadhguru urged viewing India as a civilization, not just a nation, emphasizing its spiritual and scientific heritage. He highlighted rapid global change driven by AI, stressing the need for human clarity and understanding our own potential beyond mere data processing. The conference celebrated 75 years of IITs, focusing on AI, innovation, and collaboration.

stories.title: King Charles US State visit: King to lay wreath at 9/11 memorial in New York with Zohran Mamdani
Ilhan Omar’s husband winery shuts down amid GOP probe into $30 million in couple’s assets
'Torn pants, run down car to Rs 100-crore house': Swati Maliwal's 'traitor' jibe at Arvind Kejriwal after AAP exit
stories.summary: Former aide to Arvind Kejriwal and now BJP leader Swati Maliwal has accused the ex-Delhi CM of hypocrisy, claiming he began his political journey in torn pants with a two-rupee pen and a dilapidated car, but after coming to power built a house worth Rs 100 crore.She also criticised the AAP's governance in Punjab. The remarks follow a significant party exodus.

stories.title: 'Why are there not 36, 38 or 40 cases against Mamata?' Rahul says BJP's real fight with Congress not TMC in Bengal
Russian-born British millionaire ordered to pay ex-wife £100m after secret second family uncovered
‘Get out of my country’: Elderly Sikh man physically assaulted in racist attack in Canada
3am clubs & packed roads: The stark transformation of Guwahati | I Witness
Manipur unrest: Protesters clash with police during march to CM's house
stories.summary: Protests erupted in Manipur as thousands demanded peace, clashing with security forces near the chief minister's residence. Demonstrators, organised by COCOMI, sought justice for children killed in a recent bomb blast and support for the displaced. The state grapples with escalating ethnic violence, with recent clashes claiming lives and displacing many.

Evening news wrap: Raghav Chadha loses 1 million Insta followers; Iran shares its truce demands with Pakistan

AAP implosion: BJP gains Rajya Sabha numbers, but will it be advantage Congress in Punjab?
stories.summary: The AAP, as expected, reacted very strongly to this development and accused the BJP of “Operation Lotus”, a term used to define saffron party engineered defections of political rivals. AAP leader Sanjay Singh alleged that central agencies like the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) were misused to pressure and break away AAP leaders. AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal accused the BJP of betraying Punjab, which is ruled by AAP and goes to assembly polls next year.

stories.title: Not all, but switchover of four AAP MPs to BJP cause surprise
stories.summary: This of RS MPs comes just a little over 14 months after AAP faced a rout on its homeground Delhi and when the party is bracing itself for a tough battle to save its govt in Punjab. The “defection” takes away the bounce the party enjoyed following Kejriwal’s discharge in the liquor case. The departures, besides denting AAP’s presence in Parliament also brings out its vulnerability as it now faces the big challenge of keeping its flock together — MLAs in Punjab ahead of the 2027 assembly.

stories.title: Opposition submits fresh notice seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal
stories.summary: As part of the fresh charges, the opposition has accused Kumar of “continued partisan asymmetry in enforcement of model code of conduct”, wherein it is alleged that EC failed to act on complaints against PM Narendra Modi's address to the nation on April 18 on the defeated Constitution amendment bill-related to women’s reservation amid assembly polls. CEC “has issued no show-cause notice, no advisory, and no public response” to any of the complaints made regarding this, it said.

stories.title: 44 million unknown variants: What India's Genome Project found, and why it matters
stories.summary: India has finally mapped its own DNA and what it found could change medicine for a billion people.

stories.title: NHRC flags 'inhumane' duty hours for resident doctors, seeks report from NMC in 2 weeks
Gen Z icon faces online backlash: Raghav Chadha loses over 1 million followers, flooded with hate comments after joining BJP
stories.summary: Raghav Chadha's Instagram following plummeted by over 1 million after his switch from AAP to BJP. Once a youth icon, his digital persona faced backlash, with followers expressing disappointment and betrayal. Allegations of deleting critical posts against the BJP surfaced, which Chadha denied. His appeal previously rested on addressing everyday issues, a stark contrast to his current political move.

stories.title: Iran war could push over 32 million people into poverty; UN warns of 'triple shock' for developing nations
stories.summary: A United Nations report warns the Iran war's economic fallout could plunge over 32 million people into poverty globally. Developing nations face the brunt of this crisis, grappling with surging energy and food prices. The conflict reverses development gains, pushing vulnerable populations back into destitution. Urgent global support is needed to aid these hardest-hit countries and prevent lasting damage.

stories.title: India has cut malaria cases sharply but not fully eliminated it. Where do the gaps remain?
stories.summary: Monsoon brings romanticized scenes but also a public health reality of increased malaria risk, especially for vulnerable groups. Despite significant national declines, malaria persists in localized pockets due to environmental and socio-economic factors. Climate change further complicates transmission patterns, necessitating sustained surveillance and targeted interventions for elimination.

stories.title: Blow to Kejriwal's 'dictatorship', Rekha Gupta on 7 AAP MPs' joining BJP
'Left out of disgust, not fear': Raghav Chadha attacks AAP over Sheesh Mahal 2.0 after joining BJP
stories.summary: Raghav Chadha, a prominent AAP leader, has quit the party citing disappointment and disgust, not fear, over alleged corruption and a "Sheesh Mahal" controversy. He stated that seven MPs are leaving together, believing the AAP has fallen into compromised hands. Chadha's departure follows weeks of escalating tensions and his removal as deputy leader in the Rajya Sabha.

stories.title: Christianity in decline? Study reveals one in three Britons raised Christian no longer follow the faith
'Beaten up, threatened...': After joining BJP, Swati Maliwal recalls 2024 assault at Kejriwal's house
stories.summary: Rajya Sabha MP Swati Maliwal, now with the BJP, revealed she was intimidated and threatened after alleging an assault by an AAP aide at Kejriwal's residence in 2024. She claimed immense pressure to withdraw her FIR, leading to her being sidelined by the party. Maliwal also criticized AAP's governance in Punjab and praised PM Modi's leadership.

stories.title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann seeks President Murmu's intervention after Raghav Chadha-led AAP exodus in Rajya Sabha
stories.summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann will meet President Murmu to seek the recall of seven AAP MPs, including six from Punjab, who have joined the BJP. This move follows Raghav Chadha's announcement that two-thirds of AAP's Rajya Sabha members are merging with the BJP, citing the party's deviation from its principles.

stories.title: ‘Sovereignty rests with UK’: Starmer govt rejects report of possible US ‘review’ on Falklands
'Bharatiya Jhootha Party': Sanjay Singh slams BJP over 'Sheeshmahal 2' claim, threatens defamation suits
Teen extradited from Dubai over murder of woman found dead at London home
'Only revealed Sangh’s true nature': Rahul Gandhi targets RSS after Ram Madhav’s Russia-Iran oil remarks in US
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi seized upon remarks by RSS leader Ram Madhav to criticise Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Madhav's initial comments suggested India yielded to US pressure on oil imports and tariffs, which he later retracted and apologized for. Congress claims this indicates PM Modi has lost his authority and India's sovereignty is compromised.

stories.title: Russia accuses US of energy grab, says Iran, Venezuela actions 'about oil'
stories.summary: Russia's foreign minister Sergei Lavrov has accused the US of prioritizing oil and energy dominance, alleging military actions in Iran and Venezuela are resource-driven. He claims Washington disregards international law, opting for power over rules. Lavrov urged the US towards dialogue, criticizing policy shifts that strain relations and push Europe away from Russian gas, likening it to a 'colonial era'.

stories.title: ‘Deeply unpleasant racist and Islamophobe’: UK man jailed for life for raping Sikh woman he mistook for Muslim
Telangana: K Kavitha set to launch new regional party today, pays tribute to Telangana martyrs
stories.summary: K Kavitha is launching a new political party in Telangana, aiming to fulfill the region's "unfinished agenda." She stated her supporters were expelled from the BRS, not that they left. Kavitha emphasized her deep connection to Telangana and its people, viewing them as her family, despite strained ties with her father's party and family.

stories.title: Raghav Chadha's exit: BJP releases poster mocking Arvind Kejriwal with 'AAP-da' jibe, broken broom
'Their fault': Anna Hazare holds AAP responsible over Raghav Chadha, 6 Rajya Sabha MPs joining BJP
stories.summary: Veteran activist Anna Hazare criticized AAP leadership following the departure of Raghav Chadha and six other Rajya Sabha MPs, suggesting their exit stemmed from the party deviating from its original principles. Chadha announced the group's decision to merge with the BJP, citing constitutional provisions and claiming a significant portion of AAP's Rajya Sabha members had left.

stories.title: BJP shares 'Sheeshmahal 2' pics with 'Rahman Dakait’ dig at Arvind Kejriwal; AAP calls them 'fake', asks CM Rekha Gupta to show house
stories.summary: BJP has sharply criticised Arvind Kejriwal, labelling him the "Rahman Dakait of Delhi" and accusing him of lavish living. BJP leader Parvesh Verma alleged Kejriwal built a "Sheesh Mahal 2" while Delhi suffered during the Covid wave and has now moved into a luxurious bungalow, abandoning his image of simplicity.

stories.title: Raghav Chadha-led exodus jolts AAP; party races to recalibrate strategy: What next?
stories.summary: Seven Aam Aadmi Party MPs, including Raghav Chadha, defected to the Bharatiya Janata Party, citing a deviation from the party's core principles. The move is permissible under the anti-defection law as it involves more than two-thirds of the AAP's Rajya Sabha members. AAP plans to seek disqualification for some MPs.

stories.title: Netanyahu accuses Hezbollah of 'sabotaging' Lebanon peace push
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon have extended a three-week ceasefire, with Prime Minister Netanyahu aiming for "historic peace" and crediting US pressure on Iran. Despite the truce, Hezbollah dismisses it as "meaningless" amid ongoing Israeli military actions and retaliatory clashes. This fragile calm persists amidst wider regional tensions, leaving lasting agreement prospects uncertain.

stories.title: Cub, adult tiger found dead in Kanha Tiger Reserve, Balaghat; toll rises to 23 in MP
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh has recorded 23 tiger deaths this year, with a cub found dead in Kanha Tiger Reserve and an adult tiger in Balaghat. Officials suspect starvation for the cub, whose sibling also died recently. The state, home to the country's largest tiger population, faces concerns over these fatalities and calls for improved monitoring.

stories.title: US justice dept closes criminal investigation into Fed chief Jerome Powell, clearing hurdle for Trump nominee Kevin Warsh
stories.summary: The Justice Department has closed its investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell regarding headquarters renovation cost overruns. This move removes a hurdle for Kevin Warsh's confirmation as Fed chair. The probe's closure allows scrutiny to continue through the Inspector General's office, with potential for criminal investigation restart if warranted.
